_doc.what: Curated 'mistakes never to repeat' reference (a 错题本 / lessons-learned log) for Data2Story blog generation. Each entry is a REAL bug observed in a shipped run, generalized to apply to ANY topic — not a hypothetical. The fix is the correct approach; the detect line is how a role catches it (a grep/check + the role that owns the catch).
_doc.who_reads: Programmer consults this BEFORE building (do not reintroduce a known mistake); Auditor runs each entry's `detect` during the render/static audit; Critic treats any recurring known pitfall on the page as a hard fail.
_doc.severity: hard = a defect a reader/judge can see (invisible chart, overflow, broken media, IP risk) → blocks/caps; soft = quality/polish/weight issue → advisory.
_doc.fields: id, title, symptom (what dev/reader sees), root_cause, fix (correct approach), detect (grep/check + owning role), severity (hard|soft), tags, ref (cross-link to the design ref / fix_pattern that encodes the fix).
_doc.relationship_to_quality_rubric: quality_rubric.json scores the FINISHED page PASS/FAIL per criterion; this file is the prevention log of root causes BEHIND those fails. Where a pitfall maps to a rubric criterion, the rubric criterion id is named in `ref`. Together: rubric = the gate, pitfalls = how not to trip it.
_doc.loop_rule: PROMOTE, don't just log. Once a pitfall is BINARY (a grep/file-check can decide it) or RECURRING (seen across >1 run), it must graduate from prose-only into an enforced gate — a check in inspector/scripts/validate.py and/or an Auditor `detect` step — so the pipeline catches it deterministically, not just a careful reader of this file. This file stays the human-readable root-cause ledger; the gate is the machine that can't forget. Each entry's `detect` names the owning role; an entry whose `detect` is a clean grep/stat/file-exists is a candidate to harden into validate.py.

pitfalls.title: Vega "width":"container" measured at parse time returns 0 → invisible chart
pitfalls.symptom: A chart whose CSS reads width:100% renders 0 px wide — a blank/empty box. Source inspection looks fine; the chart is simply not there in the browser.
pitfalls.root_cause: "width":"container" is measured the instant the inline <script> runs (often during page parse, before layout completes). On a long/heavy page that measurement returns 0, so Vega renders the SVG at 0 px wide.
pitfalls.fix: Embed every simple width:container chart through the canonical `embedChart` helper: measure the REAL pixel width after layout (DOMContentLoaded + requestAnimationFrame), fall back to parent width or 640 if still <40px, cap at the column max, and re-render on resize. Block-mount CSS alone (display:block; width:100%) fixes only the CSS half and is NOT sufficient.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — the live render audit reports it as zeroWidthCharts / chartsWithNoRender in render_report.json (ground truth). Static fallback: grep for `width:'container'`/`"width": "container"` and confirm the mount goes through embedChart, not a bare vegaEmbed(el, spec) call. Node/static tests CANNOT reproduce this (clientWidth returns 0 in JSDOM regardless).
pitfalls.ref: programmer component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite.responsive_embed (embed_js); auditor fix_patterns.json fix_8_chart_width_measure; quality_rubric.json CHT5

pitfalls.title: margin:auto cannot center an element WIDER than its parent
pitfalls.symptom: A breakout/full-bleed element meant to be centered instead left-aligns and overflows off the right edge; horizontal scroll appears.
pitfalls.root_cause: margin-inline:auto (and margin:0 auto) only distributes LEFTOVER space. When the element is wider than its containing block there is no leftover space, so both auto margins collapse to 0 — the element pins to the left and spills right.
pitfalls.fix: Center an over-wide element with explicit math: `margin-inline:calc((100% - min(Wpx, Nvw))/2)` (or the full-bleed idiom `width:100vw; margin-left:calc(50% - 50vw)`). Do NOT use the `transform:translateX(-50%)` hack (it leaves the layout box in place, so overflow/scroll persists).
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — render audit reports horizontalOverflow:true (desktop) or mobile.horizontalOverflow:true. Static: grep for `margin:auto`/`margin-inline:auto` or `translateX(-50%)` on any element with width >100% / width:100vw, and for left:50% hacks.
pitfalls.ref: auditor fix_patterns.json fix_center_wide_breakout + fix_5_recenter_full_bleed; layout.json full_bleed; quality_rubric.json LAY2

pitfalls.title: A Vega <svg> is wider than spec.width → overflows its card on the right
pitfalls.symptom: The rendered chart pokes past the right edge of its container/backing card; on a cinematic card the chart bleeds over the card border.
pitfalls.root_cause: Vega draws axes, axis titles and legends OUTSIDE the plotting area, so the produced <svg> is routinely wider than the `width` in the spec. The container is sized to spec.width, so the extra axis/legend overhead overflows.
pitfalls.fix: Force the rendered SVG to fit its container: `.chart-card svg{max-width:100%!important; height:auto; display:block; margin-inline:auto}` (and the same for `.vega-embed svg`). This clamps the drawn SVG to the card and centers it.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — render audit horizontalOverflow with the offending node inside a [data-des] chart; vision layout lens sees the chart crossing its card edge. Static: grep that each chart mount's shared class carries `svg{max-width:100%}`.
pitfalls.ref: auditor fix_patterns.json fix_svg_fit_container; component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite.rules (center rendered SVG); quality_rubric.json CHT5 + LAY2

pitfalls.title: Per-section dark scrim gradients create a visible horizontal seam
pitfalls.symptom: Where two sections meet over a shared photographic/cinematic background, a hard horizontal line appears — the page looks banded, not continuous.
pitfalls.root_cause: Each section paints its own dark gradient scrim for text contrast. Adjacent scrims don't line up at the boundary, so the overlap (or gap) reads as a seam.
pitfalls.fix: Use ONE uniform full-screen filter over the whole background — a single fixed overlay positioned ABOVE the background images but BELOW the content — instead of per-section scrims. If a per-image tint is needed, keep it flat and identical per image; never stack a second per-section gradient on top.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision layout/media lens sees the horizontal seam in the full-page screenshot. Static: grep for multiple per-section `linear-gradient(...rgba(0,0,0...))` scrims on consecutive sections (expect ONE fixed full-screen overlay instead).
pitfalls.ref: auditor fix_patterns.json fix_uniform_fullscreen_scrim; component_implementations.json cinematic_background; quality_rubric.json LAY5 + COL3

pitfalls.title: A data-bound render fed a null/{}-typed value → NaN/empty (radar starves bars; {value,flag} → NaN width)
pitfalls.symptom: Any data-bound visual paints nothing where a number was expected: an entity/stat card's attribute bars render at ~0 width (invisible) next to a radar; a bar's fill is missing because its width computed to NaN; a chart series / stat callout / gauge silently drops a point or shows NaN; a value-accessor returns `undefined`/`[object Object]`.
pitfalls.root_cause: A value-accessor was handed a value it can't coerce and didn't guard it. The original case: an attribute stored as a `{value, flag}` object passed to `Number({})` yields NaN, so `width:NaN%` paints nothing — but the SAME class of bug bites ANY data-bound render (chart encoding, stat callout, gauge, map marker size) when the field is null / empty-string / undefined / an object-where-a-number-is-expected, or when a baseline is rendered with a sentinel (`draw(null)` — see PIT-55 FM2). A second, layout-only compounding cause for the card case: laying a radar and the bars side-by-side in one row splits the width so the bars get almost none.
pitfalls.fix: Add ONE value-accessor used by every data-bound render that unwraps `{value}` (returns the inner number) and treats `null` / `""` / `undefined` / an object-without-a-number as MISSING — SKIP that datum rather than coercing to NaN; never `Number({…})`. Render every baseline / 'at-rest' state on REAL data, never a sentinel a callee derefs. For the card layout specifically, stack the radar ABOVE the bars (full width each), not side-by-side, so the bars get the full card width.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision lens sees zero-width/empty bars or a NaN/missing datum; render audit `findings.zeroWidthBars` is ground truth, and `findings.cascadeScriptAbort` catches the case where the null-deref actually THREW (PIT-55). The grep for `Number(`/`parseFloat(` applied to an attribute that can be an object, and for `draw(null`/`render(null` sentinel calls, is the fallback when render didn't run (checks.json check_14). Static: grep any data-bound render JS for `Number(`/`parseFloat(` on a possibly-object field, and (card case) a bars-row laid `display:flex` beside the radar.
pitfalls.ref: component_implementations.json card_decks / stat callouts + charts_vega_lite.no_sentinel_baseline_RULE; auditor checks.json check_14 + fix_patterns.json fix_10_no_sentinel_null_guard; render_capture.js findings.zeroWidthBars; cf PIT-55 (the cascade a null-deref triggers); quality_rubric.json CHT5 + LAY3

pitfalls.title: Node/JSDOM 'DOM shim' tests cannot reproduce real-browser layout
pitfalls.symptom: A static test suite passes green, but the shipped page has invisible (0-width) charts, missing bars, off-center breakouts, or overflow that the tests never caught.
pitfalls.root_cause: In a Node/JSDOM shim, `clientWidth` and `getBoundingClientRect()` return 0 (no layout engine) and `getElementById` returns a fake non-null node for anything. So width-0 bugs, null-element bugs, centering bugs and overflow bugs are all MASKED — the shim reports success.
pitfalls.fix: Use static tests for SYNTAX + LOGIC ONLY (does the JSON parse, does the function branch correctly). Visual/layout correctness MUST be verified in a REAL browser — the Auditor's headless-Chrome render audit, or a web-agent that reads actual `getBoundingClientRect()` — never a DOM shim. Treat 'static tests pass' as necessary, not sufficient.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — this is the rationale for running render_capture.js (real Chrome) as Step 0; if only static checks ran (render_audit.ran=false), layout correctness is UNVERIFIED and must be flagged as such, not assumed clean.
pitfalls.ref: auditor SKILL.md Step 0 (live render audit); checks.json (static = fallback only); quality_rubric.json CHT5

pitfalls.title: Spotify / 3rd-party audio embeds give visitors only a 30s preview and can't autoplay-from-start
pitfalls.symptom: The 'signature track' you wanted readers to hear plays only 30 seconds (for non-logged-in visitors) and can't be programmatically started from the beginning on a user gesture.
pitfalls.root_cause: 3rd-party audio embeds (Spotify et al.) gate full playback behind a logged-in account and do not expose a JS API to autoplay the full track from 0 on a visitor's first gesture.
pitfalls.fix: SELF-HOST the audio file for any 'signature track' whose playback you must control (a short, license-clean clip you own/are licensed for). Keep a 3rd-party embed only as a SECONDARY 'official version' link, never as the primary listening experience.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision/media lens + licensing check: if the primary signature audio is a Spotify/3rd-party iframe rather than a self-hosted <audio>, flag it. Static: grep for a Spotify/3rd-party iframe carrying the 'signature' role.
pitfalls.ref: component_implementations.json instance_embeds.spotify + audio recipes; motion.json accessibility.audio (audio never autoplays sound)

pitfalls.title: Browsers block autoplay-with-sound until the first USER GESTURE
pitfalls.symptom: Audio set to play on load is silently blocked; nothing is heard, and the console shows a play() promise rejection.
pitfalls.root_cause: Browser autoplay policy: audible playback is only allowed after the FIRST genuine user gesture (click / tap / keydown). Scroll and page-load are NOT gestures and do not unlock audio.
pitfalls.fix: Start audio on a user gesture, not on load: bind a ONE-TIME handler to a broad first-interaction set (`pointerdown`/`touchstart`/`keydown`/`click`) that does `audio.currentTime = 0; audio.play()`. You MAY also include `scroll`/`wheel`/`touchmove` so the score starts 'as the reader scrolls' — but a pure wheel/scroll does NOT grant audio activation, so you MUST gate on the `play()` promise: only mark it started + remove the listeners on SUCCESS, and keep listening so the next real gesture (a touch-swipe, or the first tap/key on desktop) starts it. Never bind `.play()` to load/scroll expecting sound WITHOUT that success-gate + gesture fallback. Always expose visible play/pause controls.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: grep for `.play()` bound to `load`/`DOMContentLoaded` (always wrong), or bound to `scroll`/`wheel` WITHOUT a `.then()` success-gate + gesture fallback (silently fails on desktop). Confirm <audio> has visible controls and no `autoplay` with sound.
pitfalls.ref: quality_rubric.json MOT2 (no autoplay sound; controls present); motion.json accessibility.audio

pitfalls.title: A YouTube/<iframe> is not a seamless muted hero loop
pitfalls.symptom: The hero 'background video' shows player chrome, occasional ads, and visibly restarts/jumps — it cannot loop a sub-segment seamlessly.
pitfalls.root_cause: An embedded player (YouTube iframe) is a full player, not a raw video element: it carries UI chrome, may inject ads, and cannot loop an arbitrary sub-clip cleanly. (It also fails on file:// with a null origin.)
pitfalls.fix: DOWNLOAD and re-encode a short MUTED clip and use a real `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline poster>` element for the hero. A generic, slow shot loops best (less obvious seam). Keep the source license-clean and re-encode small (see PIT-13).
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — render audit `findings.iframeHeroLoops` is ground truth; the grep for a YouTube/Vimeo iframe used as hero is the fallback. Static: grep for a YouTube/Vimeo `<iframe>` used as a hero/background (expect a self-hosted muted <video> instead); render audit console will also show the file:// null-origin error if an iframe is used.
pitfalls.ref: component_implementations.json instance_embeds.youtube (facade caveat) + cinematic background hero; quality_rubric.json MOT2 (ambient video muted + poster)

pitfalls.title: Copyrighted ratings/datasets carry IP risk AND fail the 'every number is auditable' thesis
pitfalls.symptom: A card/chart shows numbers a reader cannot trace to a public source (e.g. a game's proprietary player ratings); the work also sits on someone else's intellectual property.
pitfalls.root_cause: Lifting a proprietary index (a game's ratings, a paywalled dataset) is both an IP exposure and a violation of the Data2Story thesis that every number must be auditable — the reader cannot see WHY the number is what it is.
pitfalls.fix: Derive your OWN auditable index from PUBLIC data and PUBLISH the formula, so every number traces back to inputs. In a 'card' specifically, the real IP minefield is the VISUALS — photo license, name/likeness, club/national crests/logos — NOT the (now self-derived) number; clear those separately.
pitfalls.detect: Critic — flags any load-bearing number with no resolvable public-source lineage in verifier.json as a transparency/claim-alignment failure (caps those dimensions at 3). Auditor — licensing pass on card visuals (photo/crest/likeness rights).
pitfalls.ref: critic rubric.json data_method_transparency + claim_data_alignment; auditor SKILL.md Step 1b (image/likeness rights)

pitfalls.title: A GENERATED artifact (the inline provenance islands) desyncs after a later edit to its source
pitfalls.symptom: A derived artifact no longer matches what it was generated from: the Verify drawer shows stale/partial provenance — the inline `verifyMap` / `runCells` <script type="application/json"> islands no longer reflect verify/*.json on disk.
pitfalls.root_cause: The inline islands are GENERATED, not hand-authored: they are embedded copies of verify/verify_map.json + verify/run_cells.json. Any later edit to the SOURCE (an index.html change, or a verify_map.json / run_cells.json change) shifts/desyncs the previously-generated copy. The page reads the INLINE/GENERATED copy, so the on-disk source being correct is not enough.
pitfalls.fix: Regenerate every derived artifact as the VERY LAST step, after all source edits (Auditor fixes, Critic send-back fixes, cleanup) are final: re-run generate_viewer.py so the `verifyMap`/`runCells` islands are re-inlined FROM the canonical verify/*.json and each island is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its source file. Never hand-edit a generated artifact to 're-sync' it.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector — re-run generate_viewer.py as the final step so the islands are re-inlined from verify/*.json. Auditor — static: extract each inline `verifyMap`/`runCells` island and byte-compare it to verify/verify_map.json / verify/run_cells.json; flag any mismatch. If any role edited a source after its artifact was built, the artifact is stale.
pitfalls.ref: inspector role (viewer generation as final step); inspector_panel_internals.json (inline_byte_identical); validate.py dangling-tag check (PIT-12)

pitfalls.title: Hand-built modules whose data-* tags aren't in the role JSONs → validate.py dangling-tag errors + broken overlay
pitfalls.symptom: validate.py reports dangling-tag errors; the inspector audit overlay highlights nothing (or errors) on those hand-built modules.
pitfalls.root_cause: Every `data-edt/-des/-ana/-sct/-cin` attribute is expected to resolve to a record in the corresponding role JSON. A module authored by hand (or copied) with tags that don't exist in editor.json/designer.json/analyst.json/scout.json/cinematographer.json leaves dangling references.
pitfalls.fix: Every `data-*` traceability tag MUST resolve to a role-JSON record. When you hand-build a module, ADD the matching record to the owning role's JSON (or run a re-sync pass that reconciles tags ↔ JSON). Keep them in sync; don't ship orphan tags. Multiple IDs of one kind go in ONE attribute, comma-separated with no spaces (data-det="det_02,det_05") — validate.py splits on commas, so a space-separated value is flagged dangling; connective [editorial] paragraphs carry no data-ana/data-det.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — run validate.py; dangling-tag errors list the unresolved attributes. Static: grep index.html for every `data-(edt|des|ana|sct|cin)=` value and confirm each appears as an id in the matching role JSON.
pitfalls.ref: validate.py (dangling-tag check); programmer traceability.json (every visual tagged + resolvable)

pitfalls.title: Orphaned/scratch media + un-encoded big assets (incl. raw generated video) bloat page weight
pitfalls.symptom: The page payload is large (slow mobile load): the assets/ folder contains raw downloads, replaced/duplicate assets, and oversized originals; a generated hero/AI video ships at its raw 20–30 MB instead of a web-delivery weight.
pitfalls.root_cause: Intermediate downloads and superseded assets are never cleaned up, and large originals (hero video, hero image, full-quality audio) ship un-re-encoded. A video generator routinely returns a large MP4 (20–30 MB) that gets referenced directly, never transcoded — so total payload balloons.
pitfalls.fix: Run a CLEANUP + TRANSCODE pass before ship: keep exactly ONE signature audio + ONE hero video; delete orphaned/scratch/replaced media; re-encode big media. For ANY video (sourced OR generated) transcode to web weight before shipping — a <3 MB H.264 mp4 + a webm twin via ffmpeg — and reference the WEB copies, not the raw original (install `static-ffmpeg` if ffmpeg is absent — it provides ffmpeg + ffprobe, cf PIT-14). Compress images, lazy-load below-the-fold images. Target the budget (audio ≤ 3 MB, image ≤ 600 KB, video ≤ 3 MB, total ≤ ~8 MB).
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — render audit reports oversizedAssets / performance.totalOverBudget (send-back to Designer for generated media, Scout for sourced media). Static: list/stat assets/ and flag files over budget, and any referenced hero/AI video > 3 MB; confirm the page references the transcoded web copy (mp4 < 3 MB + a webm twin), not the raw generator output. For UNREFERENCED assets specifically: an unreferenced heavy master in `assets/` is RELOCATED to `provenance/` by the Inspector finalize step (`inspector/scripts/relocate_unreferenced.py`, run at Stage 7); `validate.py` Section 16 (`asset_unreferenced_heavy`) ERRORs if any unreferenced heavy file remains in `assets/` after relocate — no longer merely flagged.
pitfalls.ref: auditor SKILL.md (oversized_asset send-back + performance budget); media_presentation.json (lazy-load, re-encode); validate.py Section 16 (asset_unreferenced_heavy); inspector/scripts/relocate_unreferenced.py (Stage-7 finalize relocate of unreferenced heavy masters to provenance/); cf PIT-14 (static-ffmpeg)

pitfalls.title: yt-dlp needs BOTH ffmpeg + ffprobe; imageio-ffmpeg lacks ffprobe
pitfalls.symptom: yt-dlp fails during post-processing (merge/convert) with a missing-ffprobe error, even though an ffmpeg binary is present.
pitfalls.root_cause: yt-dlp's post-processing needs both `ffmpeg` AND `ffprobe`. The `imageio-ffmpeg` package ships only the ffmpeg binary (no ffprobe), so yt-dlp can't probe streams.
pitfalls.fix: Install a bundle that provides BOTH: `pip install static-ffmpeg` (gives ffmpeg + ffprobe), and pass `--ffmpeg-location` to yt-dlp pointing at that bundle's bin directory.
pitfalls.detect: Scout/pipeline — when a media download via yt-dlp errors on ffprobe, this is the cause; confirm both binaries are on the path / passed via --ffmpeg-location before retrying.
pitfalls.ref: scout media-acquisition tooling; validate.py media gate

pitfalls.title: Required facts may be ABSENT from the dataset — source them, never fabricate
pitfalls.symptom: A planned element needs a fact the dataset doesn't contain (e.g. geo-coordinates for a map, venue capacities, a date) and the value isn't in any data_table.
pitfalls.root_cause: The provided dataset is incomplete for the intended story element; the missing fact (coordinates, capacity, etc.) simply isn't there to resolve from analyst.json.
pitfalls.fix: Source and VERIFY the missing facts SEPARATELY from an authoritative reference (Wikidata / Wikipedia / official source) and record their provenance. NEVER fabricate or guess a number to fill the gap — an unsourced number fails the auditability thesis.
pitfalls.detect: Critic — any on-page number with no resolvable source lineage caps transparency/claim-alignment at 3. Analyst/Scout — flag dataset gaps and attach the external source + URL for each backfilled fact.
pitfalls.ref: critic rubric.json data_method_transparency; analyst.json (provenance per fact); find-data completeness gates

pitfalls.title: A clean 'signature' real-video loop may not exist as a sustained shot
pitfalls.symptom: No single continuous clip is long/steady enough to loop as a seamless hero background; every real cut shows a visible jump at the loop point.
pitfalls.root_cause: Real footage rarely contains a long, static, cut-free shot suitable for a seamless background loop; the obvious clip is too short or too dynamic.
pitfalls.fix: Build a seamless loop from a short clip via slow-motion + a forward-reverse 'boomerang' (play then reverse), so the end frame returns to the start frame and the loop point is invisible. Keep it muted and re-encoded small (see PIT-09 / PIT-13).
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision/media lens watches the hero for a visible jump at the loop seam. Cinematographer — own this when sourcing the hero loop.
pitfalls.ref: cinematographer hero-loop recipe; component_implementations.json cinematic_background hero video

pitfalls.title: A card deck mixing real photos and silhouettes looks unfinished
pitfalls.symptom: Some entities in a card deck show a real photo and others show a generic silhouette/placeholder — the deck reads as half-done.
pitfalls.root_cause: Photos were sourced for only some entities (license gaps, missing assets), leaving placeholders that visually advertise the gap.
pitfalls.fix: Source a REAL, license-clean photo for EVERY entity in the deck — or DROP the entity entirely. Do not ship a deck where the presence/absence of a photo is uneven.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision/media lens sees the mix of photos and silhouettes across the deck. Static: grep the deck for placeholder/silhouette asset names alongside real photos. Scout owns sourcing the missing photos.
pitfalls.ref: scout image sourcing; quality_rubric.json ANT5 (no decorative/placeholder filler); component_implementations.json card_decks

pitfalls.title: Multiple persistent UI controls pinned to the SAME viewport corner overlap
pitfalls.symptom: Two (or more) always-on controls — e.g. a 'Verify' toggle and an audio/BGM bar, or a hero 'Real/AI' toggle and a scroll-progress control — sit on top of each other in a screen corner; one hides, clips, or blocks clicks to the other. (NOTE: there is NO cinematic on/off toggle — the cinematic stage is unconditional — so it is never one of the colliding controls.)
pitfalls.root_cause: Each control was given its corner anchor independently (e.g. both `position:fixed`/`absolute` at `top:1rem; right:1rem`). Nothing coordinates their placement, so they land at identical coordinates and collide — and the higher z-index one can make the other unreachable.
pitfalls.fix: Give the page ONE corner-control plan: put global controls in DIFFERENT corners (e.g. Verify top-left, audio bar top-right), and when two must share a corner, stack them with an explicit offset (`top:1rem` and `top:3.9rem`) — never identical coordinates. A section-scoped control (e.g. a hero-only Real/AI toggle) must sit clear of the global fixed controls, including on mobile. Re-audit corners after ADDING any new fixed/absolute control.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision/layout lens sees the overlapping controls in the corner screenshot. Static: grep for >=2 elements with `position:fixed`/`position:absolute` sharing the same corner anchors (e.g. multiple `top:1rem;right:1rem`), at both desktop and the mobile breakpoint; confirm each has a distinct corner or an explicit stacking offset.
pitfalls.ref: component_implementations.json toggles/controls placement; quality_rubric.json LAY-series (no overlapping/obscured UI controls)

pitfalls.title: Front-of-blog BGM player left-pinned/buried instead of centered at the top below the title, or its cover is a static square instead of a spinning vinyl disc
pitfalls.symptom: The BGM/soundtrack player sits flush-left in the column (off-centre), or appears partway down the article instead of at the very opening — it reads as a stray widget rather than the page's 'press play and read' invitation. OR its cover is a plain static square that gives no signal the track is playing.
pitfalls.root_cause: The player card has a max-width but no centering (e.g. `margin:0 0` instead of `margin:0 auto`/`margin-inline:auto`), and/or it was placed in a mid-article section rather than the opening below the title; and/or the cover was left a static square rather than the canonical spinning vinyl disc.
pitfalls.fix: Place the soundtrack/BGM player at the VERY TOP of the article, directly BELOW THE TITLE (the opening content block) AND horizontally CENTER it (`margin-inline:auto`, centered in the column) on every breakpoint, so the reader can start it before reading — a top-of-article card guarantees the reader notices the BGM (this is the CANON; it is NOT a fixed top-right corner widget). Render the cover as a SPINNING VINYL DISC: the cover art clipped to a circle (`border-radius:50%`) that rotates ONLY while playing (CSS @keyframes + animation-play-state, paused otherwise; `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` disables the spin), with title + artist + a play/pause button. Reader-controlled, never autoplay sound. (BGM is mandatory on every blog — cf PIT-29-style absence; the classical-recording floor guarantees a clean track always exists.)
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision/layout lens checks the opening: is the player centered and at the top below the title, with a circular spinning-disc cover? Static: grep the soundtrack/BGM player card for a `max-width` WITHOUT `margin:auto`/`margin-inline:auto` (left-pinned), confirm the audio item is the first content block / its section is the opening, and confirm the cover carries `border-radius:50%` + an `animation-play-state`-driven spin gated on a `.playing`/playing state (not a static square).
pitfalls.ref: designer audio_rules.json (sourced_bgm: centered card at the very top below the title + cover_treatment spinning vinyl disc); components.json signature_media_card.vinyl_cover; programmer component_implementations.json audio_music.sourced_bgm (spinning-disc CSS); quality_rubric.json LAY-series

pitfalls.title: Multi-asset media collapsed to the FIRST asset / one aggregate credit → only one item shown + verifiable
pitfalls.symptom: An element backed by several assets (a flag set, a photo/face deck, a logo set) shows or credits only ONE of them: either the renderer drops every asset after the first, or the deck carries a single summarised credit ('images via …') instead of a traceable source+license per asset. Either way a reader cannot see or verify the individual items.
pitfalls.root_cause: Two facets of the same mistake: (a) RENDER — the media renderer used `firstUrl(source_url)` / `[0]` (took only the first entry) instead of iterating the gallery array, so assets after the first are lost; (b) PROVENANCE — credit was attached at the DECK level, not the ITEM level, collapsing each asset's source+license into one summary line.
pitfalls.fix: Treat any `flags` / `assets` / `photos` array as a GALLERY end-to-end: render every asset with its OWN thumbnail + label, AND attach every asset's OWN source + license (a per-item `photos[]` gallery on the element). So each face / logo / flag is both VISIBLE and INDIVIDUALLY verifiable. Never reduce a multi-asset entry to its first URL, and never summarise a deck's provenance into one aggregate credit string.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: (a) grep the media/render JS for `firstUrl(`/`[0]` applied to a `source_url`/`assets`/`flags`/`photos` array, and confirm multi-asset entries map over the WHOLE array (one credited thumbnail per asset); (b) for any card/photo deck confirm the element exposes a per-item `photos[]`/gallery with a source+license per asset, not one aggregate credit for the whole deck.
pitfalls.ref: verify_map.schema.json ($defs/galleryItem); inspector_panel_internals.json (gallery); quality_rubric.json A11Y1 (per-asset alt/credit)

pitfalls.title: In-browser (Pyodide) "run it yourself" snippet not self-contained / uses unavailable imports / runs full-N
pitfalls.symptom: A 'run it yourself' code snippet hangs or throws in the browser: it tries to read files or hit the network, imports a package Pyodide doesn't ship, or attempts the full-N computation and never returns.
pitfalls.root_cause: Pyodide runs in the browser sandbox: it has no local files / network by default and only a limited package set, and full-N compute blocks the main thread. Snippets written like a local script fail there.
pitfalls.fix: Make each runnable snippet SELF-CONTAINED + REDUCED-N + Pyodide-safe: inline all inputs (no file/network reads), import only numpy / pandas / stdlib, and run heavy compute at a reduced N graded "≈ within noise" (NEVER a hard PASS) with the full-N version kept in the notebook. If a cell `needs_network:true` then `runnable:false` — show it read-only and point to the notebook.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: parse run_cells.json (and the inline runCells island) and flag any runnable snippet whose imports are outside {numpy, pandas, stdlib}, that reads files/network, or that has `needs_network:true` while still `runnable:true`. Reduced-N cells must be graded '≈ within noise', not PASS.
pitfalls.ref: run_cells.schema.json

pitfalls.title: Animating a real person's face (image2video) risks uncanny warping
pitfalls.symptom: An image2video pass on a real, identifiable face produces uncanny deformation — the face warps/melts as the motion is generated.
pitfalls.root_cause: Generative motion deforms a real identifiable face; the model reshapes features it should leave fixed.
pitfalls.fix: Keep the real face STILL — animate only the stage / atmosphere around it — or use a strict no-warp motion prompt and REJECT any candidate that distorts the face. Fall back to a still face if no clean motion candidate passes.

pitfalls.title: verify_map.json is the provenance source-of-truth and may legitimately REPOINT a coarse on-page data-* tag
pitfalls.symptom: An element's `data-ana` (or other `data-*`) points at a finding that isn't its true source — e.g. a card grid carries a neighbouring analysis id because one coarse tag covers a mixed region.
pitfalls.root_cause: The on-page `data-*` tag is necessarily coarse (one id per region), so it can name a finding adjacent to, but not exactly, the element's real source.
pitfalls.fix: Let `verify_map.json` carry the CORRECT provenance for that id and record the correction in an `_note`; keep the map AUTHORITATIVE over the raw on-page tag. The repoint is legitimate — do not 'fix' it by forcing the tag to match.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — treat verify_map.json as authoritative when its provenance for an id differs from the coarse on-page `data-*` tag; confirm any such repoint is documented in an `_note` rather than flagged as a dangling/incorrect tag.
