pitfalls.title: Verify layer silently absent — the whole coding-verifier layer vanishes on a fresh run
pitfalls.symptom: A shipped run has NO verify layer at all: no `verify/` directory, no `#verifyToggle` / Inspector panel in index.html — yet the run was presented as finished. The paper's mandatory coding verifier is simply gone, and nothing hard-failed.
pitfalls.root_cause: The verify layer was 'MANDATORY' in prose only. The Programmer's Step 2.5 (authoring the panel shell + `verify/` payloads) and the Inspector's Stage 7 (`generate_viewer.py`, which fills the islands) sit OUTSIDE the Critic loop, and the older contract gate (validate.py) checked only `data-*`↔role-JSON, never the verify layer — so a run that skipped Step 2.5 + Stage 7 still passed every hard gate.
pitfalls.fix: Make the layer a HARD pipeline gate, redundantly on both the deterministic and the LLM side. Deterministic (authoritative): validate.py Section 7 asserts the `verify/` files exist + the panel shell is pasted (Stage-6 contract gate), and generate_viewer.py must exit 0 at Stage 7. LLM-side net (this pitfall): the Critic HARD-fails a page missing the verify layer and CAPS `data_method_transparency` at 3, sending the fix to the Programmer (Step 2.5). A run is INCOMPLETE if the layer is absent — never present it as finished.
pitfalls.detect: Critic — confirm the verify layer is PRESENT (not filled): (1) the FILES exist — `verify/verify_map.json`, `verify/run_cells.json`, and exactly one `verify/*.ipynb`; AND (2) index.html carries the panel SHELL — a `#verifyToggle` control PLUS the two island `<script type="application/json">` tags (`id="verifyMap"` and `id="runCells"`). IMPORTANT (stage timing): the Critic runs BEFORE Stage 7 fills the islands, so the islands are legitimately EMPTY at Critic time — do NOT require their contents to be non-empty (that would hard-fail every run). Check shell-present + files-exist only. The deterministic island-FILLING gate is validate.py Section 7 (files + shell) + generate_viewer.py (fills + exits nonzero on any gap) at Stage 7. If the FILES or the SHELL are missing → HARD fail, cap `data_method_transparency` at 3, send back to Programmer (Step 2.5). Static greps: `ls PROJECT_DIR/verify/verify_map.json PROJECT_DIR/verify/run_cells.json PROJECT_DIR/verify/*.ipynb`; `grep -n 'verifyToggle' PROJECT_DIR/index.html`; `grep -nE 'id="verifyMap"|id="runCells"' PROJECT_DIR/index.html`.
pitfalls.ref: data2story/SKILL.md Stage 7 (REQUIRED terminal step, MUST exit 0) + contract-gate verify_* routing; inspector/scripts/validate.py Section 7 (files + panel shell); inspector/scripts/generate_viewer.py (Stage 7 island-fill, nonzero exit on gap); critic rubric.json data_method_transparency (runnable coding verifier); cf PIT-11 (island byte-identity / generated-artifact desync, a DIFFERENT — filled-state — check)

pitfalls.title: A purposeless supporting playground — a widget that teaches the reader nothing
pitfalls.symptom: An interactive is on the page but produces no cognitive update: it re-teaches the hero's finding, the reader drives a control and learns nothing new, or it was added because 'more interactives is better.' It looks busy but earns nothing.
pitfalls.root_cause: Abundance was pursued without the quality gate. A supporting playground was built with no DISTINCT finding it lets the reader produce/feel, or it duplicates the hero centerpiece, so it is decoration that happens to move.
pitfalls.fix: Every supporting playground MUST declare an explicit INFORM or IMMERSE purpose bound to a DISTINCT finding (no two playgrounds share one finding; none re-teaches the hero). The kill-rule stands: kill any interaction that doesn't change what the reader understands. More is NOT better — the curated SET (hero + supporting) survives only when EACH earns its place; an unearned widget caps visual_design at 3. Cut it at the media-purpose gate before the Programmer builds it.
pitfalls.detect: Critic — for each supporting playground, confirm interaction.json/editor.json declares a purpose (INFORM/IMMERSE) bound to a finding distinct from the hero and from every other supporting; a playground with no purpose, a duplicate finding, or one the reader can't produce anything from is a hard fail (caps visual_design/insight_value at 3, send to the Critic/Editor-curation loop). The media-purpose gate (data2story SKILL.md) cuts a purposeless playground BEFORE it is built.
pitfalls.ref: critic rubric.json R8 + insight_value.common_failure; interaction_playbook.json centerpiece_doctrine.earned_test/anti_pile; report_types.json interaction_purposeless; quality_rubric.json ANT5

pitfalls.title: A dead control — a slider/button that does nothing (only a real browser catches it)
pitfalls.symptom: A playground's control looks live but driving it changes nothing: the slider moves but the readout/chart is static, the button click is a no-op, or the control throws in the console. The reader produces nothing.
pitfalls.root_cause: The control is wired wrong (no handler, a handler bound to the wrong element, a recompute that errors) — OR it was only ever tested in a Node/JSDOM shim where a synthetic event 'passes' and getBoundingClientRect/clientWidth read 0, so the dead control is masked (cf PIT-06). A synthetic .click() also can never move a native <input type=range>, so a range-driven widget shows identical before/after under a naive probe.
pitfalls.fix: Drive every control in a REAL browser: set range/number values + dispatch BOTH 'input' and 'change' (a click won't move a native range), advance selects with 'change', .click() buttons — then read the DECLARED [data-play-out] readout (not whole-container innerText). A control whose declared readout never changes, or that errors when driven, is a dead control → hard send-back to the Programmer. NEVER certify interactivity from a static/shim test.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — the Playtester (playtest_drive.js, Step 0c) drives each [data-int] in real Chrome and reports checks.fires==FAIL (readout unchanged or console error in that step) as interaction_dead_control. Node/JSDOM shims CANNOT reproduce this (events 'succeed', layout reads 0). With no browser the check is UNVERIFIED, never PASS.
pitfalls.ref: auditor/scripts/playtest_drive.js (fires check); cf PIT-06 (shim masks dead controls); report_types.json interaction_dead_control; quality_rubric.json A11Y3 + LAY3

pitfalls.title: A playground recomputes a DIFFERENT number than the published headline
pitfalls.symptom: At rest (untouched widget) the interactive's live in-browser readout disagrees with the published figure the prose claims — e.g. the article says 26.3% but the explorable's baseline shows 31%. The reader 'runs it themselves' and gets a contradicting number.
pitfalls.root_cause: The inlined client_model / data_table the playground recomputes from drifted from the audited Analyst figure (a stale constant, a different seed, a wrong reduced-N, or a divergent formula), so the Python→JS-live layer no longer converges to the published number. The three-layer-number standard is broken at the JS layer.
pitfalls.fix: Seed the playground at the AUDITED baseline so the untouched widget reproduces the headline EXACTLY (derived: equal to display precision; stochastic: '≈ within noise' at reduced N against the published figure, NEVER a hard PASS). The same audited client_model feeds the headline AND the live readout (same_model_as_headline). If they disagree, fix the inlined model/data_table — do not 'fix' the published number to match a broken widget.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — the Playtester's recompute_oracle check (playtest_drive.js, Step 0c) reads the baseline live readout and compares it to the published data_table figure (exact within a small epsilon for derived; within a declared Monte-Carlo band, median of 2–3 samples, for stochastic). A disagreement is interaction_recompute_disagrees → hard send-back to the Programmer. This closes the Python→JS-live→Pyodide loop no other gate checks.
pitfalls.ref: auditor/scripts/playtest_drive.js (recompute_oracle); flagship_contract.json interactive_supporting_set; report_types.json interaction_recompute_disagrees; cf PIT-23 (Pyodide reduced-N '≈ within noise'); critic rubric.json claim_data_alignment

pitfalls.title: A playground breaks with JS/CDN off — no static fallback reveals the number
pitfalls.symptom: With JavaScript disabled, a blocked CDN (Vega/D3/Pyodide fails to load), or reduced-motion, the interactive collapses to an empty box and the at-rest number is simply gone — a reader on a flaky network or restrictive browser sees nothing where the finding should be.
pitfalls.root_cause: The playground renders its number ONLY via JS; there is no server-rendered/static at-rest value, no <noscript>, no `if(!MODEL){…show the published number;return}` guard, so any JS/CDN failure erases the load-bearing figure.
pitfalls.fix: Every playground degrades gracefully: ship a <noscript> + an `if(!MODEL){render the published static number; return}` path + a prefers-reduced-motion path, AND keep the at-rest number in the STATIC DOM (so a blocked CDN still shows it). The enhancement is interactive; the baseline number must survive JS-off.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — the Playtester's degradation check (playtest_drive.js, Step 0c) re-renders the page with JavaScript DISABLED and confirms the at-rest number is in the [data-int] static text, plus a <noscript>/reduced-motion path exists. A playground that shows no figure JS-off is interaction_no_degradation → hard send-back to the Programmer.
pitfalls.ref: auditor/scripts/playtest_drive.js (degradation); interaction_playbook.json (<noscript>+reduced-motion fallback per recipe); report_types.json interaction_no_degradation; quality_rubric.json MOT1/MOT6

pitfalls.title: A pile of widgets with no clear hero — abundance with no focal centerpiece
pitfalls.symptom: The page stacks many interactives of equal weight with nothing dominant — a widget grid, not a story. The reader can't tell which one is THE explorable; the article reads as a toy box, not a guided argument.
pitfalls.root_cause: Supporting playgrounds were added without preserving exactly ONE hero centerpiece the narrative is built around. 'More interactives' became the goal, flattening the hierarchy so no single playground anchors the page (the LAY3/ANT3 focal-point failure, in interactive form).
pitfalls.fix: Keep exactly ONE hero centerpiece (the single contestable headline number, placed at/before the reveal, the narrative built around it) + any number of supporting playgrounds that each earn their place in their bound section. The hero must visibly dominate; supporting playgrounds stay subordinate. A widget-pile with no clear hero caps insight_value at 3.
pitfalls.detect: Critic — confirm there is exactly ONE hero centerpiece that anchors the page and that supporting playgrounds are subordinate, not co-equal; a flat pile with no dominant interactive is a hard fail (caps insight_value at 3, send to the Critic/Editor-curation loop). cf LAY3/ANT3 (a soulless even grid with no focal point), here applied to the interactive set.
pitfalls.ref: critic rubric.json R8 + insight_value; interaction_playbook.json centerpiece_doctrine (exactly ONE hero); quality_rubric.json LAY3 + ANT3; report_types.json interaction_purposeless

pitfalls.title: AI-generated track used as the front-of-blog BGM
pitfalls.symptom: The page's soundtrack is a text2music / Lyria-composed track presented as the main BGM. It reads as generic mood-wash, not a real piece of music tied to the story, and there is no real artist/cover to credit.
pitfalls.root_cause: An older framing treated AI-generated music as the BGM 'default'. text2music's strength is atmospheric beds, not a front-of-blog soundtrack; a composed track has no real provenance, no cover art, and nothing auditable to credit — it cannot anchor the page the way a real sourced track does.
pitfalls.fix: The front-of-blog BGM MUST be a REAL sourced track in the signature_media_card cover-art card (a SPINNING VINYL DISC cover + title/artist/one-line desc + a single play/pause button, at the top of the article below the title) that autostarts on the reader's first gesture (the sndKick 7-window-event, lock-on-success, currentTime=0 pattern). Use a license-clean track when one fits (publishable); a best-fit copyrighted track may be self-hosted for the DEMO as a des_ asset with publish_blocker:true (Auditor advisory copyrighted_audio_publish_blocker + a footer 'demo-only — license or swap before publishing' note), never claimed as a clean sct_. When no topic-fitting or signature track exists, the GUARANTEED license-clean floor is a CLASSICAL RECORDING (verify the RECORDING's license, not just the composition's PD status; period-appropriate or a famous master, mood-appropriate) — so there is ALWAYS a real clean BGM and never a reason to reach for an AI track. text2music is SFX-only — the opt-in sound_design/SFX form for an un-findable sound (a drone, a texture, a scene bed), short and reader-controlled, NEVER the BGM.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: grep the front-of-blog BGM player; if its <audio> src is a text2music/generated asset (a designer generated-audio item used as the masthead BGM) rather than a sourced_bgm/real-track asset, flag it. Confirm the BGM renders as the signature_media_card cover card with the first-gesture autostart, not a generated mini-player. cf PIT-07/PIT-08 (self-host + gesture-gated) and PIT-19 (centered at the top).
pitfalls.ref: components.json signature_media_card (primary BGM cover card) + audio_player.sound_design (SFX form); programmer component_implementations.json audio_music.sourced_bgm (cover card + sndKick) / sound_design; designer audio_rules.json (BGM = sourced, text2music = SFX); auditor flagship_contract.json bgm_music + report_types.json copyrighted_audio_publish_blocker

pitfalls.title: Veo / Wan image2video HARD-REFUSE a real, identifiable celebrity face
pitfalls.symptom: An image2video job whose source still contains a recognizable real person (a footballer, an actor, a politician) is REJECTED by the model — not a bad render, an outright policy refusal. Veo returns error code 15236754 (likeness/safety block); Wan refuses similarly. The pipeline stalls on the hero with no clip.
pitfalls.root_cause: Veo (and Wan) enforce a likeness/safety policy that blocks animating a real identifiable face. seedance does NOT refuse but it MOVES the subject (deforms/repositions the face, cf PIT-27). So the two 'default' image2video paths each fail a faces-still cinemagraph: one refuses, the other warps.
pitfalls.fix: For a hero that must keep a real face STILL while only the scene moves (a faces-still cinemagraph), use Kling (kling v3 std worked for the flagship) — it animates atmosphere around a held face without the hard refusal. Reserve seedance/text2video for GENERIC, no-real-face motion. If every faces-on model refuses or warps, fall back to the still image (poster) — never ship a warped face. (For the model-list/duration constraints when calling these, see PIT-39.)
pitfalls.detect: Cinematographer/Designer — when an image2video submit returns a likeness/safety refusal (Veo code 15236754) on a real-face source, this is the cause: switch the model to Kling for the faces-still beat rather than retrying Veo/Wan. Auditor — vision lens still checks the resulting clip for a warped face (cf PIT-27).
pitfalls.ref: data2story/designer/scripts/openrouter-image2video (model selection); cf PIT-27 (face-warp on animation), PIT-39 (video model list + duration), PIT-16 (seamless loop)

pitfalls.title: Kling caps output at 720p — native-rendering a 'hi-res' hero gives a soft, sub-HD clip
pitfalls.symptom: A hero cinemagraph rendered through Kling tops out at 720p; requesting 1080p/4K natively is ignored or errors, and the full-bleed hero looks soft on a large screen.
pitfalls.root_cause: Kling's image2video output resolution is capped at 720p. There is no native high-res render to ask for — the ceiling is the model's, not a parameter you set.
pitfalls.fix: Render at Kling's 720p, then AI-UPSCALE the finished clip to the delivery resolution as a separate post step (see PIT-38 for the upscaler gotcha) — do NOT try to native-render above 720p. Then transcode the upscaled clip to web weight (PIT-13). Order: generate 720p → upscale → transcode → ship.
pitfalls.detect: Cinematographer/Designer — if a hero clip is soft/sub-HD straight from Kling, confirm an upscale post-step ran (not a failed attempt to native-render >720p). Auditor — vision lens flags a soft full-bleed hero; static: hero pipeline should show a 720p render + an upscale stage.
pitfalls.ref: cinematographer hero pipeline; cf PIT-38 (Real-ESRGAN tile bug), PIT-13 (transcode after upscale)

pitfalls.title: Real-ESRGAN ncnn-vulkan 2× has a tile-scramble bug → use 4× then lanczos-downscale
pitfalls.symptom: Upscaling a clip/frame with Real-ESRGAN ncnn-vulkan at scale 2× produces visible tile artifacts — the image is scrambled into mismatched square blocks at tile seams.
pitfalls.root_cause: The ncnn-vulkan build of Real-ESRGAN has a known tile-handling bug at the 2× scale: tiles are stitched wrong, so the output is block-scrambled. The 4× path does not hit the bug.
pitfalls.fix: Never request 2× from Real-ESRGAN ncnn-vulkan. Upscale at 4× (x4plus, which is clean) and then LANCZOS-DOWNSCALE to the target size you actually wanted (e.g. 4× then ÷2 for an effective 2×). The 4×→downscale route avoids the tile scramble and yields a clean result.
pitfalls.detect: Cinematographer/Designer — if an upscaled frame/clip shows square tile artifacts, you ran 2×; switch to 4×→lanczos-downscale. Auditor — vision lens flags block/tile artifacts on an upscaled asset.
pitfalls.ref: cinematographer/designer upscale step; cf PIT-37 (why upscaling is needed at all)

pitfalls.title: OpenRouter lists video models ONLY at GET /api/v1/videos/models; duration is 4/6/8 only
pitfalls.symptom: Picking a video model from OpenRouter's normal model list fails — the chat /models endpoint omits video models entirely, so a valid video model id 'doesn't exist'. Separately, a video job with duration 5 (or any non-{4,6,8}) is rejected.
pitfalls.root_cause: OpenRouter splits its catalog: the standard `GET /api/v1/models` (chat) list does NOT include video models. Video models are enumerated ONLY at the separate `GET /api/v1/videos/models` endpoint. And the video generation API accepts ONLY duration values 4, 6, or 8 seconds — arbitrary durations error.
pitfalls.fix: Discover a video model via `GET /api/v1/videos/models` (NOT the chat /models list), then submit to `POST /api/v1/videos`. Set `duration` to exactly 4, 6, or 8 — never an in-between value. Bake both facts into the generation tooling so a model lookup and a duration choice are valid on the first call.
pitfalls.detect: Cinematographer/Designer/pipeline — if a video model id is 'not found', confirm the lookup hit `/api/v1/videos/models`, not `/api/v1/models`; if a job errors on duration, confirm duration ∈ {4,6,8}. Static: grep the video tooling for the `/api/v1/videos/models` listing call and a duration constrained to 4/6/8.
pitfalls.ref: data2story/designer/scripts/openrouter-image2video + openrouter-text2video (config.json endpoints; add the /videos/models listing + duration∈{4,6,8} guard)

pitfalls.title: Head-to-head % (sums to 100 between two) conflated with championship % (out of N)
pitfalls.symptom: A number reads as wrong or contradictory because two different probabilities are shown without saying which space they live in — e.g. a 'pick a side' two-way share (Argentina 58% vs France 42%, summing to 100) sits next to the model's championship odds (Argentina 26.3%, out of 48 teams), and a reader thinks the page contradicts itself.
pitfalls.root_cause: Two probabilities from DIFFERENT sample spaces were presented as if comparable: a head-to-head/conditional share normalizes between just two outcomes (sums to 100% across the pair), while a championship probability is out of the whole field of N (sums to 100% across all teams). Unlabeled, the head-to-head number looks like an inflated championship number.
pitfalls.fix: Always LABEL which probability space a number lives in, right where it is shown: 'X% to win the World Cup' (out of all teams) vs 'X% vs France' / 'X% of this pair' (head-to-head). Keep the two visually + verbally distinct, and when an interaction reveals a championship figure, converge it on the model's published out-of-N value (not a two-way share). One number, one named denominator.
pitfalls.detect: Critic/Auditor — for every probability on the page, confirm its denominator/space is stated or unambiguous from context (championship out-of-N vs head-to-head pair). Flag any two probabilities placed side by side that imply different spaces without labels. cf PIT-42 (the figure must read from the model, not a hardcoded literal).
pitfalls.ref: interaction_playbook.json content_patterns (label the comparison); critic rubric.json claim_data_alignment; cf PIT-42

pitfalls.title: Decorative overlay (chips, particle canvas) swallows interaction clicks or becomes a spurious Verify hit-target
pitfalls.symptom: A purely decorative layer over an interactive hero intercepts the reader's clicks — the 'pick a side' halves or the Verify hit-target stop responding where a chip/canvas sits — OR a decorative chip carries a data-* tag and so lights up as a (meaningless) Verify provenance target.
pitfalls.root_cause: A decorative overlay (an EA-style ability chip, a particle <canvas>, a flourish) was given default pointer behaviour and/or a stray data-* attribute. With pointer events on, it eats clicks meant for the interactive layer beneath it; with a data-* tag, the Verify engine treats it as a real provenance hit-target.
pitfalls.fix: Every DECORATIVE overlay MUST be `pointer-events:none` AND carry NO `data-*` traceability tag (and usually `aria-hidden="true"`). Then clicks pass through to the real interactive/Verify layer beneath, and Verify never offers a meaningless decorative target. Only genuine content/controls get pointer events + data-* tags. (cf the inverse pitfall PIT-12: real modules MUST have resolvable data-*; decorative ones must have NONE.)
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: for each absolutely/fixed-positioned overlay above an interactive region (chips, canvas, flourishes), confirm it sets `pointer-events:none` and has no `data-(edt|des|ana|sct|cin|det|int)=` attribute. Playtester — if a hero control fails to fire only in the region under an overlay, suspect a decorative layer eating the click.
pitfalls.ref: exemplars/cinematic_flagship.md (E1 pick-a-side hero: decorative chips pointer-events:none + NO data-*); cf PIT-12 (real modules need resolvable data-*); quality_rubric.json A11Y3

pitfalls.title: A displayed number hardcoded as a literal instead of read from the model at runtime
pitfalls.symptom: An on-page figure (a championship %, a stat, an interactive readout) is written into the HTML/JS as a constant. It silently goes STALE the moment the model/data changes, and an interaction that 'reveals' it shows a number the live model never produced — breaking the auditability promise.
pitfalls.root_cause: The figure was typed in as a literal (a magic number in markup or a JS constant) rather than read from the page's own model/data at runtime. The displayed value and the model can then drift apart, and the reader 'running it themselves' gets a different number.
pitfalls.fix: Displayed numbers MUST read from the model/data at runtime — derive them from the inlined client_model / data_table / a `window.MODEL.*` accessor, never a hardcoded literal in markup or script. The ONLY place an expected number lives as a literal is provenance/expected_stdout (the verify layer's recorded oracle for grading), NOT the rendered page. Seed an interaction's at-rest readout from the same model so it reproduces the headline by construction (cf PIT-32: a widget recomputing a DIFFERENT number than the headline).
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: grep the markup/JS for load-bearing numbers (percentages, headline stats, interaction readouts) typed as literals rather than read from the model/data accessor; confirm the at-rest readout is sourced from the model, with literals confined to verify/expected_stdout. Playtester recompute_oracle (PIT-32) catches a live value that disagrees with the published figure.
pitfalls.ref: exemplars/cinematic_flagship.md (E1/E2: every number read from window.WC_MODEL / accuracyData, none hardcoded); interaction_playbook.json centerpiece_doctrine.same_model_as_headline; cf PIT-32 (recompute disagrees), PIT-40 (label the probability space)

pitfalls.title: Hero→content transition reads as a shrinking rectangle over a fixed backdrop
pitfalls.symptom: As the reader scrolls from the hero into the first section, the hero doesn't dissolve away — it visibly SHRINKS, a rectangle scaling down over a static background. The transition looks like a collapsing pane / a closing window, not a continuous film handing off to the next scene.
pitfalls.root_cause: The transparent hero OVERLAY (the `.teaser` carrying the furniture, sitting over a fixed/pinned background video) was animated out with `transform:scale()` (e.g. a `.leaving{transform:scale(.92)}` or a scroll-driven scale). Scaling a TRANSPARENT overlay does not move the fixed backdrop behind it, so the eye sees the overlay's box shrink against an unmoving background — a shrinking-pane seam. Scale only looks continuous on SOLID full-bleed media that fills the frame; on a see-through overlay it exposes the trick.
pitfalls.fix: Dissolve the hero overlay with OPACITY ONLY (no scale): drive `hero.style.opacity` 1→0 on scroll progress and let the existing crossfade engine carry `cin_00 → cin_01` behind it (put the hero video in the backdrop stack as `cin_00`, cf the E5 hero-as-cin_00 recipe). NEVER apply `transform:scale()` to a transparent overlay. Only ever scale SOLID full-bleed media (a ken-burns on a background image/video that fills the viewport), never a transparent furniture overlay. Under reduced-motion, early-return and leave the overlay fully opaque.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision lens watches the hero→first-section scroll for a shrinking rectangle instead of a dissolve. Static: grep the hero scroll handler / CSS for `transform:scale(` or a `scale(` applied to the `.teaser`/hero OVERLAY element (the transparent furniture layer), and confirm the overlay's scroll-out animates `opacity` only — not transform. Cinematographer/Programmer own the hero handoff.
pitfalls.ref: exemplars/cinematic_flagship.md (E5 hero-as-cin_00 continuous backdrop handoff: overlay dissolves by opacity only, GOOD-vs-BAD shrinking-pane); cinematographer cinematic_recipes.json (hero_as_cin_00 / continuous pinned backdrop); cf PIT-04 (per-section scrim seam), PIT-09/PIT-16 (hero loop)

pitfalls.title: Interactive hero halves built as <button>/<a href> land in the Verify allow-list → container drawer never opens
pitfalls.symptom: Under Verify-ON, clicking a 'pick a side' hero half does nothing useful: the hero stops opening its provenance drawer, OR the click is consumed by the half and never reaches the container's Verify hit-target. The reader can play the hero OR inspect it, but the two fight — the interactive hero and the click-to-source Verify layer don't coexist.
pitfalls.root_cause: The clickable halves were authored as `<button>` or `<a href>` elements, which ARE in the Verify engine's `INNER_INTERACTIVE` allow-list. The Verify engine treats an allow-listed inner control as a real interactive leaf and lets its click run (or the element's own default/handler consumes it), so the gesture never bubbles up to the CONTAINER that carries the provenance `data-*` Verify needs to open the drawer.
pitfalls.fix: Build the halves as `role="link"` elements (NOT `<button>`/`<a href>`) — `role="link"` is NOT in the Verify `INNER_INTERACTIVE` allow-list, so the click bubbles to the container. Then: (1) EVERY half handler's FIRST line is `if (verify-on) return;` (so under Verify-on the gesture passes through to the container instead of mutating the hero); (2) feature code NEVER calls `stopPropagation`/`preventDefault` on the bubbling click (the bubble to the container is load-bearing — it's how Verify gets the gesture); (3) the provenance `data-*` lives on the CONTAINER (`.teaser`), not on the halves; decorative overlays on top carry `pointer-events:none` + no `data-*` (cf PIT-41). Real interactive CONTROLS that should NOT bubble (a slider/button inside a supporting widget) stay `<button>/<input>` — this rule is specifically for the two big hero hit-areas that must ALSO be the container's Verify target.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: grep an interactive hero (a `.teaser`/centerpiece that also needs a CONTAINER Verify hit) for `<button` or `<a href` used as the big clickable halves/hit-areas (expect `role="link"` instead), confirm every half handler early-returns under verify-on, and confirm NO `stopPropagation`/`preventDefault` in the hero feature code. Playtester (Step 0c verify_coexist) drives the hero under Verify-on and fails it if the drawer doesn't open. Interaction/Programmer own the coexistence wiring.
pitfalls.ref: exemplars/cinematic_flagship.md (E1 interactive 'pick a side' hero that coexists with Verify: role=link halves, early-return guard, no stopPropagation, data-* on container); interaction/references/interaction_recipes.json (verify_coexistence); auditor flagship_contract.json interactive_hero_verify_coexistence (report_type interactive_verify_coexistence_broken); cf PIT-41 (decorative overlay eats clicks), PIT-31 (dead control / verify_coexist)

pitfalls.title: A RICH topic took the impoverished path (1 image, cinematic off, static hero, generic-loop BGM) yet passed every gate
pitfalls.symptom: A genuinely visual/computational topic ships threadbare — one stock image, cinematic mode off, a flat static cover photo, and a generic topically-unrelated CC0 loop for BGM — and NOTHING flags it: zero validation errors, every hard gate green. The run is presented as 'done' even though it under-delivered at every richness decision, because the pipeline rewards omission (the safe minimal path) rather than richness.
pitfalls.root_cause: The gates were built to cut EXCESS (the media-purpose gate kills purposeless additions) but had no floor against IMPOVERISHMENT: each step independently chose the cheapest safe option (Scout sourced 1 image, the Cinematographer fell back to off, the cover stayed a static still, the soundtrack stayed a generic loop) and each choice passed its own local check. With no richness floor reading the topic profile, a rich topic that owes a dynamic hero + cinematic + an asset floor + a best-fit soundtrack can satisfy every gate while delivering none of them.
pitfalls.fix: Enforce a richness FLOOR keyed off topic_profile (the inverse of the media-purpose gate): the richness checks ERROR on a topic the classifier marks visual/computational, WARN otherwise — so when topic_profile.is_visual==true OR is_computational==true the impoverished path is BLOCKED (sent back), and on any other topic it is a warning, never silently shipped (absent-profile / privacy-sensitive are exempt). On a visual topic that means a dynamic hero (not a bare static still), cinematic ON when supply exists, a license-clean topic-asset floor (>=3 distinct, >=5 cover-able for cinematic), and the best-FIT real soundtrack (rung 2 climbed, not a generic loop). Each required-rich element still earns its place via the existing purpose gates — the floor forbids impoverishment, it never forces a fabricated/decorative asset (which itself caps visual_design at 3). The richness verdict cross-references the already-hard computational floors (substantive verify, >=1 earned interactive) so one 'richness' read covers all of it.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py richness_* checks (richness_cinematic_undersupplied / richness_static_hero / richness_asset_floor / richness_hollow_verify_cells) load topic_profile and ERROR on a topic the classifier marks visual/computational, WARN otherwise (absent-profile / privacy-sensitive exempt). Orchestrator — the richness gate (data2story SKILL.md, beside the media-purpose gate) surfaces 'richness floor not met' in the closing summary; on a topic the classifier marks rich it blocks (sends back) unless a legitimate blocker is recorded, rather than reporting a silent 'done'. Critic — on a visual topic the impoverished path (1 image + no cinematic + static hero + generic-loop BGM) caps visual_design at 3 (inverse of the decorative-media cap).
pitfalls.ref: validate.py Section 12 (richness_cinematic_undersupplied / richness_static_hero / richness_asset_floor / richness_hollow_verify_cells + topic_profile loader); data2story/SKILL.md richness gate; auditor flagship_contract.json (cinematic_supply_floor / dynamic_hero_on_visual / topic_asset_floor, complement of missing_engagement_floor); critic rubric.json visual_design + insight_value richness-floor cap; cf PIT-46 (cinematic dropped for lack of supply), PIT-47 (generic loop where a real anthem fits), PIT-48 (an ABSENT topic_profile no-ops this whole floor — now a hard error); the engagement half of the impoverished path (a descriptive topic shipping NO earned interactive) is now a HARD block-with-escape — validate.py Section 12 missing_engagement_floor + flagship_contract.json missing_engagement_floor

pitfalls.title: Cinematic under-supplied on a visual topic — settle for a non-photographic fallback instead of sending Scout back for >=5
pitfalls.symptom: On a clearly visual topic the Cinematographer ships a non-photographic fallback (generative / data_driven) and the run accepts it as 'the correct outcome' — but the reason is UNDER-SUPPLY (Scout sourced only 1-4 cover-able backgrounds), not that the topic is genuinely abstract. The richer PHOTOGRAPHIC scroll the topic warranted is quietly absent and nothing sends the pipeline back to source more imagery. (Historically this surfaced as the now-retired mode:off; cinematic is now mandatory, so the under-supply shows up as a fallback mode, not an off.)
pitfalls.root_cause: The under-supply fallback was treated identically to an honest-abstract fallback. Scout sourced too few cover-able images, the Cinematographer correctly cannot run a photographic scroll on 1-4 backgrounds, and the older guidance called any fallback 'the correct outcome' — so the fix (go get more imagery) was never triggered. The >=5 threshold existed but nothing enforced sending Scout back to meet it.
pitfalls.fix: Discriminate honest-abstract fallback (correct restraint on a weakly-visual topic — passes) from under-supply fallback (impoverishment on a visual topic — sent back). When is_visual AND cinematic is ON (any on-mode) AND 1 <= (verified license-clean cover-able image count) < 5: warn-and-send-back — Scout sources >=5 (ideally a dozen+) cover-able backgrounds and the Designer registers each as des_/sct_ BEFORE the Cinematographer re-runs, so the immersion can UPGRADE to photographic. The image COUNT is the primary signal (the 1<=count<5 bound prevents firing on zero / privacy-sensitive imagery); the mode_reason is only a secondary confirm. The >=5 threshold itself is unchanged; only the response to an under-supplied immersion changes from 'silent, correct' to 'send back to source first'.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py richness_cinematic_undersupplied (the supply half of the richness floor: is_visual ∧ cinematic ON ∧ 1<=cover-able-count<5 -> send-back). Cinematographer/Scout/Designer own the re-source loop. Orchestrator — the cinematic-supply gate bullet surfaces the send-back.
pitfalls.ref: validate.py Section 12 (richness_cinematic_undersupplied); scout/SKILL.md + designer/SKILL.md + cinematographer/SKILL.md (reword 'correct outcome / silent' -> 'on a visual topic an under-supplied off is sent back to source >=5 first'); auditor flagship_contract.json cinematic_supply_floor; cf PIT-45 (the whole impoverished path), PIT-16 (a clean seamless loop may not exist)

pitfalls.title: A generic CC0 loop shipped where a real recognizable anthem was the best fit — rung 2 not climbed
pitfalls.symptom: A story that HAS a signature track (an official anthem, a film theme, the song the piece is about) ships a generic, topically-unrelated CC0 loop as its BGM instead, on the reasoning that the clean loop is 'license-clean and publishable.' The reader hears mood-wash with no connection to the story, and the real best-fit track the piece is literally about is absent.
pitfalls.root_cause: License-tier was treated as the PRIMARY selector instead of a tiebreak: a license-clean loop won simply because it was publishable, even though it fit the story far worse than the real anthem. The audio ladder's rung 2 (a best-fit copyrighted track self-hosted for the demo behind a publish-gate) was not climbed — the pipeline settled for the clean loop on rung 1 although the loop fit worse. FIT FIRST was inverted into LICENSE FIRST.
pitfalls.fix: FIT FIRST: pick the most recognizable best-FIT real track the story carries; license-tier is a tiebreak ONLY among comparably-fitting tracks. When the story has a signature anthem/theme/song, SOURCE THAT — climb to rung 2 (a des_ audio asset with publish_blocker:true, license 'All Rights Reserved — demo-only', source_url, demo-gated) rather than substituting a generic clean loop. A license-clean track wins only when it fits the story AS WELL as the best-fit one (then publishable breaks the tie). The rung-2 publish-gate stays loud (Auditor advisory copyrighted_audio_publish_blocker + a 'demo-only — license or swap before publishing' footer); the answer to the IP tension is the gate, not a worse-fitting loop. A generic clean loop in place of the real best-fit anthem is NOT a win just because it is publishable. NOTE: when the story has NO signature track AND no topic-fitting real track, the GUARANTEED clean floor is a license-clean CLASSICAL RECORDING (mood/period-appropriate, recording's license verified) — that floor is the right clean fallback, NOT a generic unrelated CC0 loop.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — static: when the story carries a signature track (a det_/scout-noted official anthem/theme/song) confirm the BGM is that best-fit track on rung 2 (a des_ asset with publish_blocker:true) or rung 1 only if a clean track fits AS WELL, NOT a generic topically-unrelated CC0 loop. Designer/Scout own the FIT-FIRST track choice. cf PIT-35 (BGM must be a REAL sourced track, never AI-composed) and PIT-07 (self-host the signature track, not a 30s embed).
pitfalls.ref: designer audio_rules.json (default / bgm_ladder rungs 1-2 / copyrighted_referenced_track: FIT FIRST, license-tier is a tiebreak; rung 2 carries publish_blocker:true + publish_note); scout/SKILL.md + designer/SKILL.md (reorder preference: source the signature anthem); components.json signature_media_card; cf PIT-35 (no AI BGM), PIT-45 (the whole impoverished path)

pitfalls.title: topic_profile absent -> the richness/cinematic/BGM/engagement floors all silently no-op (a stale gate read the template, not the resolved profile)
pitfalls.symptom: A blog ships with no per-run topic_profile authored (neither detective.json nor scout.json carries explicit is_visual + is_computational), and NOTHING flags it: every capability-gated floor (richness_*, cinematic_missing, bgm_missing, missing_engagement_floor) reads falsy and quietly does not fire, so a rich topic can ship impoverished while every gate stays green. A sibling failure: a flagship_contract trigger that greps the references/topic_profile.json TEMPLATE side-file (an examples wrapper with no top-level booleans) instead of the resolved profile, so the trigger reads nothing and the floor is dead.
pitfalls.root_cause: The shared classifier was treated as ABSENT-FALSE: validate.py resolved topic_profile to {} on 'nothing found' and every downstream check used `bool(tp.get('is_visual'))`, which cannot distinguish 'no profile authored' (absence) from 'profile authored all-false' (an honest abstract topic). With no presence check, a genuinely absent profile silently disabled the entire richness family. Separately, gates that read the references/topic_profile.json template (which carries no top-level is_visual/is_computational — only an examples/template wrapper) read nothing and no-op'd.
pitfalls.fix: Treat topic_profile as RESOLVED only when BOTH capability keys are explicitly PRESENT (`'is_visual' in tp AND 'is_computational' in tp` — key presence, NOT truthiness), so an honest is_visual:false,is_computational:false topic counts as resolved (and correctly trips none of the floors) while a genuinely ABSENT profile is a HARD ERROR. The Detective (Stage 1) MUST write a resolved topic_profile{is_visual,is_computational,tags[]}; the Scout (1.5) writes it if the Detective did not. Every gate reads the RESOLVED profile in detective.json/scout.json (including the post-Analyst is_computational upgrade), NEVER the references/topic_profile.json template (which only widens/labels).
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py raises `topic_profile_unresolved` (error, unconditional — the one richness-family check that is NOT capability-gated) when neither detective.json nor scout.json carries a topic_profile with explicit is_visual + is_computational. Auditor — confirm every flagship_contract trigger greps detective.json/scout.json for the resolved profile, not the template side-file. Static: `grep -nE '"is_visual"|"is_computational"' PROJECT_DIR/detective.json PROJECT_DIR/scout.json` returns a real per-run profile.
pitfalls.ref: validate.py Section 0b (topic_profile_unresolved, key-presence resolver) + Section 12 (the capability-gated floors it guards); auditor flagship_contract.json _doc.trigger_inputs.topic_profile (read the resolved profile, not the template); cf PIT-45 (the impoverished path a no-op'd floor lets through), PIT-46

pitfalls.title: A malformed verify_map entry passes the Stage-6 contract gate, then crashes generate_viewer.py at Stage 7
pitfalls.symptom: validate.py reports a clean verify layer at the Stage-6 gate (verify/ exists, panel shell pasted, every page id has a map entry), but the terminal Stage-7 step (generate_viewer.py) then exits nonzero on a per-kind schema violation — a verify_map entry with an unknown/absent `kind`, a non-object value, or a kind missing a required key. The run looked green at the gate and only blew up at the very end.
pitfalls.root_cause: The Stage-6 gate (validate.py Section 7) asserted the verify_map PARSES + has >=1 key + every page data-* id is a key, but it did NOT mirror generate_viewer.py's VERIFY_MAP_REQUIRED per-kind required-key check. So a structurally-malformed entry slipped through the gate and was only caught by generate_viewer.py's validate_islands() at Stage 7 (which exits nonzero), after the gate had already passed.
pitfalls.fix: Mirror generate_viewer.py's VERIFY_MAP_REQUIRED (the per-kind required-key dict for computation|media|generated|fact|credits) at the Stage-6 gate, kept in LOCK-STEP with the Stage-7 source. validate.py Section 7 now walks every authored verify_map entry and fails it AT THE GATE — a non-object entry, an unknown/absent kind, or a kind missing required keys — so a malformed map routes back to the Programmer (Step 2.5) before Stage 7 instead of crashing it. The on-disk verify_map.json is authored complete at Step 2.5, so this is safe pre-island-fill (it inspects the authored entries, not the empty page islands). The five kinds are complete; a decorative gradient carries no data-* token and so has no entry.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py raises `verify_map_entry_malformed` (entry is not an object), `verify_map_unknown_kind` (kind not in computation|media|generated|fact|credits), or `verify_map_kind_keys_missing` (a known kind missing a required key) at the Stage-6 gate. generate_viewer.py validate_islands() remains the Stage-7 backstop. Static: confirm validate.py's VERIFY_MAP_REQUIRED equals generate_viewer.py's (they will drift if edited apart).
pitfalls.ref: validate.py Section 7 (per-kind VERIFY_MAP_REQUIRED mirror); inspector/scripts/generate_viewer.py VERIFY_MAP_REQUIRED + validate_islands (the Stage-7 source of truth); verify_map.schema.json $defs (the five kinds + decorative_no_entry note); cf PIT-29 (verify layer silently absent), PIT-11 (island byte-identity)

pitfalls.title: data_driven cinematic mode DECLARED but never BUILT — the chart-spine immersion is absent and nothing flags it
pitfalls.symptom: cinematographer.json sets meta.mode == "data_driven" (the chart-spine scroll background for an abstract topic), but the immersion was never produced: no built scene exists (scenes is empty, or every scene is image/video), or scenes exist but the page carries no data-cin token wiring the scroll layer. Because a data_driven scene carries no media_ref, validate.py Section 6's per-scene media_ref guard never fires, so the declared-but-not-built immersion ships silently.
pitfalls.root_cause: Section 6 only validated image/video scenes (their media_ref must resolve); a data_driven chart-spine / gradient scene has NO media_ref by design, so it was entirely unguarded. A mode declared in meta but with no built scene and/or no data-cin on the page is the gap the media_ref guard cannot see.
pitfalls.fix: When meta.mode == "data_driven", assert >=1 real BUILT scene AND that the page wires the scroll layer. 'Built' is defined by INVERSION — any non-_ scene whose background.kind is NOT image/video (color/gradient/chart/...) — so an unanticipated non-media kind still counts as built (no false-positive). If no built scene exists -> send back to the Cinematographer (the declared immersion was never produced); if built scenes exist but no data-cin token is on the page -> send back to the Programmer (the scroll layer is not wired). The render QUALITY of the built layer stays an Auditor/Critic concern (flagship_contract cinematic_background); this only catches declared-but-utterly-absent.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py raises `cinematic_data_driven_not_built` (Section 6b) with `where` disambiguating Cinematographer (cinematographer.json, no built scene) vs Programmer (index.html, built but no data-cin). Static: when `grep -nE '"mode"' PROJECT_DIR/cinematographer.json` shows data_driven, confirm >=1 non-image/video scene exists AND `grep -n 'data-cin' PROJECT_DIR/index.html` returns a real token.
pitfalls.ref: validate.py Section 6b (cinematic_data_driven_not_built); auditor flagship_contract.json cinematic_background (the mandatory-mode-declared-but-not-built half; QUALITY cap stays Critic); cinematographer/references/schema.json (data_driven = chart-spine, no media_ref); cf PIT-45 (impoverished path), PIT-46 (under-supply fallback)

pitfalls.title: A "scout."-prefixed data_source silently bypassed the designer cross-reference check (a dangling free-text reference shipped unflagged)
pitfalls.symptom: A designer item's content.data_source is a free-text `scout.<something>` string (e.g. scout.live_status for a dated reality-check strip). validate.py Section 3 saw the `scout.` prefix and skipped the reference ENTIRELY — so a typo'd or dangling scout.<suffix> that resolves to nothing still passed the gate, while a normal data_source (an ana_ id) is checked. The bypass swallowed every scout.-prefixed reference, resolving or not.
pitfalls.root_cause: Section 3's data_source check excluded any string starting with `scout.` from the analyst-id resolution (an unconditional bypass, because a scout.* reference is not an ana_ id), but it never positively RESOLVED the scout.* suffix against anything — so the prefix was an escape hatch that disabled the check rather than redirecting it.
pitfalls.fix: Resolve a `scout.<suffix>` data_source instead of bypassing it: accept it when the suffix names a registered scout item (suffix in sct_ids, or 'sct_'+suffix in sct_ids), OR when it is `scout.live_status*` and scout.json carries a non-empty top-level `live_status` list (the dated display-only reality-check strip); otherwise it is a dangling reference and errors. The observed real grammar is unambiguous (scout.live_status, backed by a real live_status list), so this resolves correctly without false-positiving a legitimate blog.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py raises `des_data_source_scout_dangling` (Section 3) when a designer content.data_source starts with `scout.` but its suffix resolves to neither a registered sct_ item nor a non-empty live_status in scout.json. Static: `grep -nE '"data_source":\s*"scout\.' PROJECT_DIR/designer.json` and confirm each suffix resolves in scout.json.
pitfalls.ref: validate.py Section 3 (des_data_source_scout_dangling resolver); cf PIT-12 (every data-* / cross-reference must resolve to a role-JSON record, no orphan references)

pitfalls.title: A subtle cinemagraph hero reads as a STATIC photo + has no seamless loop — technically-correct video that looks dead
pitfalls.symptom: The cover is a real <video autoplay loop muted> with correct attributes, yet a reader sees what looks like a still: the only motion is a 'faint pulse' / 'thin clouds drift slowly' over an otherwise-static stadium/building, so the page reads as one more static-photo blog. Separately, the raw model clip VISIBLY JUMPS at the loop point (head and tail don't connect), a cut every few seconds. The cover — the page's single most load-bearing detail and its hook — squanders the animated treatment.
pitfalls.root_cause: Two compounding misses. (a) Motion too SUBTLE: the image2video prompt asked only for minimal-motion verbs (a faint pulse, a slow drift) instead of a clearly-visible PRIMARY motion + strong SECONDARY motions, so the cover never reads as alive. (b) No SEAMLESS LOOP: the model clip was shipped raw, with no boomerang/crossfade post-process, so frame N != frame 0 and the loop jumps. (A subject that TRANSLATES across/off the frame — a train driving off-screen — also cannot loop and compounds it.)
pitfalls.fix: Make the cover DRAMATIC + LOOPED. (a) Require a clearly-visible PRIMARY motion + 1-2 strong SECONDARY motions, all IN-PLACE / cyclic (flags WAVING boldly, wheels SPINNING, smoke BILLOWING, crowd SURGING, sky parallax) — when the subject must stay still (building/landscape/held face) the motion comes from a BOLD animated foreground, never a faint pulse; never translate the subject off-frame (pick the concept from hero_recipes.json topic_motion_library). (b) Post-process EVERY hero clip into a seamless loop — default ffmpeg BOOMERANG (`[0]reverse[r];[0][r]concat`, inherently seamless), alt CROSSFADE the loop point (`xfade`, last ~0.5s into first ~0.5s) — and RECORD the technique on hero.json `loop` ("boomerang"|"xfade"|"native"); resolve ffmpeg via the imageio-ffmpeg wheel (not on PATH). Keep the on-page `loop` attribute.

Hero/Designer own the dramatic-motion + seamless-loop fix.

pitfalls.title: Verify panel / fixed overlay white-out: an unpainted <html> root + no color-scheme:dark + a backdrop-filter:blur toggle flushes the dark page to the UA-white root canvas on a light OS theme
pitfalls.symptom: A reader on a light OS theme (or certain GPUs/zoom levels) opens the Verify panel — or merely loads a page with a fixed blurred control — and the dark page blows out to ALL-WHITE / unreadable. The panel's own CSS is all-dark and cannot be reproduced headlessly; the page looks fine for most readers, so it ships unnoticed.
pitfalls.root_cause: The emitted page paints `<body>` dark but leaves `<html>` UNPAINTED (e.g. only `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}`) and never declares `color-scheme:dark`, so the ROOT canvas is the UA default — white under a light UA color-scheme. A fixed element with `backdrop-filter:blur(...)` / `-webkit-backdrop-filter` (the `.verify-toggle`, a sticky bar, a `.v-backdrop`) samples whatever is painted behind it; with the unpainted white root as the backdrop, Chromium can flush the whole page to white (a documented backdrop-filter + unpainted-root quirk). The verbatim panel template shipped this vector every run (dark `<body>`, unpainted root, blurred toggle).
pitfalls.fix: Belt-and-suspenders, all three: (1) PAINT THE ROOT dark — `:root{ color-scheme: dark; background: var(--bg); }` (or `html{background:var(--bg)}`) and/or `<meta name="color-scheme" content="dark">`, so the root canvas is never the UA white. (2) DECLARE color-scheme:dark on the real page (its theme comes from the Designer's page_rhythm, so the fix must land in the actual `<head>`, not only the demo template). (3) GUARD THE BLUR — either drop `backdrop-filter` (the toggle already has a solid `background:rgba(20,18,16,.82)` fallback) or wrap it in `@supports (backdrop-filter:blur(6px))` with the solid background as the base, so no fixed element ever blurs against an unpainted root.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector — validate.py Section 7f raises `root_color_scheme_missing` (no `:root/html{...color-scheme:dark...}` rule and no `<meta name="color-scheme" content="...dark...">`) and/or `root_background_unpainted` (no `html`/`:root` background rule — only `<body>` painted) on the emitted index.html. WARN (robustness floor). Static: the page paints a `<body>` background but no `html`/`:root` background, declares no color-scheme, AND carries a `backdrop-filter`/`-webkit-backdrop-filter` fixed element — that triad is the white-out vector. The white-out itself is NOT headlessly reproducible (it needs a light OS theme + certain GPUs); painting the root + declaring color-scheme + guarding the blur neutralizes the only plausible vector. Programmer/Designer own painting the root in the real theme.
pitfalls.ref: inspector/references/inspector_panel_reference.html (:root color-scheme:dark + html{background} + @supports-guarded .verify-toggle backdrop-filter); programmer/SKILL.md Step 2 (paint <html>/:root dark + color-scheme:dark, not just <body>); validate.py Section 7f (root_color_scheme_missing + root_background_unpainted); cf PIT-18 (corner controls overlap — the same fixed-overlay family), PIT-06 (real-browser-only render truth)

pitfalls.title: Near-black gradient REST creates a black scroll gap in photographic cinematic mode (a photo ends -> black -> long scroll -> next photo)
pitfalls.symptom: In the scroll-driven cinematic background the reader hits black/empty stretches between photos: a photo ends, the page goes near-black, a long scroll passes with nothing on screen, then the next photo arrives. The scroll coverage is continuous (no dead zones) and validate.py is green — the holes are gradient 'rest' scenes rendering as near-black sections, sometimes two back-to-back, so the background looks broken even though every gate passes.
pitfalls.root_cause: In PHOTOGRAPHIC mode (which HAS real verified imagery) a 'rest' beat was emitted as a `kind:gradient` scene — a near-black `linear-gradient(#0c0d11 -> #111319)` full-bleed layer with NO — exactly like a generative/data_driven rest. validate.py Section 6 deliberately SKIPS color|gradient scenes (legitimate in the abstract modes), so the near-black rest passes every check; and two such rests can land consecutively, doubling the dead stretch. A bare gradient is the right rest medium ONLY when there are no real photos (generative/data_driven) — in photographic mode it IS the black gap.
pitfalls.fix: Redefine a photographic rest so the background stays a REAL photo, never bare black: a rest beat HOLDS the previous/upcoming verified sct_/des_ image as a quieter beat — reuse the existing `framed` blurred-fill treatment (the blurred-darkened cover copy `filter:blur(~32px) brightness(~.45)`, optionally the contained image dimmed) and/or a heavier scrim — so the same photographic surface simply quiets down and one photo flows seamlessly into the next. Keep the silky crossfade (CSS-transition opacity restart + img.decode(), no `void offsetWidth` reflow). FORBID in photographic mode: (a) any `kind:gradient`/`kind:color` rest, and (b) two consecutive rest scenes. Gradient/atmospheric rests stay valid ONLY in generative/data_driven mode (no real photos exist there).
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py Section 6c raises `cin_photographic_gradient_rest` (a cin scene with background.kind gradient|color while meta.mode is photographic/cinematic) and `cin_consecutive_gradient_rests` (two adjacent gradient rests) — ERROR, photographic mode only (the existing Section-6 gradient SKIP stays for generative/data_driven). Auditor — checks.json check_13_photographic_gradient_rest_black_gap greps cinematographer.json for a gradient/color `kind` under a photographic mode and index.html for two adjacent `.cin-bg` layers painting a CSS gradient with no data-sct/data-des. Vision/media lens sees the black stretch in the full-page screenshot. Cinematographer owns redefining the rest; Programmer owns rendering the dimmed real-photo layer.

pitfalls.title: One uncaught throw in the shared <script> blanks every sibling chart + the hero (cascade abort)
pitfalls.symptom: A whole page of charts goes blank at once — not one bad chart, but every chart AND the hero render nothing — and the console shows a single error like `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'datum')`. Source inspection of each chart looks fine in isolation; the data is inlined; yet nothing paints below the point of the throw.
pitfalls.root_cause: All chart/interaction setups are emitted into ONE shared inline `<script>` that runs each setup SEQUENTIALLY. A single synchronous uncaught exception (the classic trigger: a baseline `draw(null,…)` / `render(undefined)` sentinel the callee derefs, or `Number({value,flag})` on an object — see PIT-05) aborts the ENTIRE `<script>` block, so every setup AFTER the throw — including later charts, later playgrounds, and the hero wiring if it sits below — never runs. The existing `embedChart` `.catch()` only wrapped the `vegaEmbed()` promise, NOT the synchronous `specFn(cw())` / data-prep that runs before it, so a throw there still escaped. Highest blast radius of any chart bug: one line takes down the page.
pitfalls.fix: FAULT-ISOLATE every setup. Wrap each chart's and each playground's WHOLE setup in its own IIFE `(function(){ try { /* build spec / state + render() + wireControls() */ } catch(e){ console.error('<id> setup', e); } })();` so a throw logs to console and the NEXT setup still runs. `embedChart` now also wraps its whole body (incl. the data-prep + the embed call) and degrades to a static table when the CDN is blocked. Pair with PIT-05's no-sentinel-baseline + null/`{}` guards (FM2) so the throw is prevented at source, and wrap feature-side handler bodies in try/catch (FM5) so a reader gesture can't throw into the event loop either.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — render_capture.js findings.cascadeScriptAbort is ground truth: it correlates >=1 console error with >=2 charts that rendered nothing and emits ONE finding (so it routes as a single send-back, not N blank-chart reports). Static fallback (no browser): validate.py Section 14 WARNs `chart_no_fault_isolation` — a single `<script>` mounting >=2 charts/interactions (vegaEmbed/setup) with <1 `try` (ERROR on a computational/rich topic); checks.json check_14 greps the same. Programmer owns wrapping each setup; the fix composes with PIT-05.

pitfalls.title: Templated / AI-tell headline — the 'flat statement. flat counter-statement.' two-beat (AT1) reads as machine-written
pitfalls.symptom: The page H1 (or a section heading) sounds like an LLM wrote it, not a newsroom: most often the AT1 two-beat — a flat declarative sentence followed by a short contradicting one ("Argentina is the favourite. No bookmaker agrees.") — or a topic label instead of a conclusion ("An Analysis of …", "Exploring …", "A Look at …"), an empty superlative the data doesn't back, or a colon subtitle reflex ("Topic: A Something of Something"). The headline names the SUBJECT and hides the FINDING.
pitfalls.root_cause: Titling was left to a competent default, which reaches for the AI-tell patterns the Copywriter's AT1-AT9 kill-list names — above all the AT1 two-beat, the rhythm no human editor writes but an LLM produces every time. The headline was written front-to-back (from the topic) instead of last, from the conclusion backward, and only one phrasing was generated instead of several across different devices.
pitfalls.fix: Run the Copywriter (Stage 3.5): write the headline LAST, from the conclusion backward; generate SEVERAL candidates across different devices (D1-D16) and pick the strongest; state the so-what (the conclusion), not the topic; concrete noun + vivid verb + real number; honest promise, not clickbait; statement not Betteridge question. KILL the AT1 two-beat first — rewrite "X. Not Y." into a single device-driven spine ("Every bookmaker has Argentina behind the model"). The Copywriter writes copywriter.json (strings only, each backed by a real ana_*); the Programmer renders masthead.headline + section titles verbatim. (Naming, not editing — no finding/number/id changes.)
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — checks.json check_15_titling_caption_quality greps the <h1> / masthead.headline for the AT1 'statement. short counter-statement.' shape and the templated roots ('An Analysis of', 'A Look at', 'Exploring', 'Understanding', a reflexive colon subtitle, a marketing word). Critic — corroborates via rubric.json narrative_pacing.titling_caption_cap (a generic/templated headline caps narrative_pacing at 3, send back to copywriter). ADVISORY (soft) — not a hard gate and not a validate.py kind yet (so it stays out of the deterministic contract gate until proven); promote to a validate.py Section only after the grep is shown two-sided.

pitfalls.title: Standfirst pre-spoils the interactive hero's reveal number — the centerpiece has nothing left to deliver
pitfalls.symptom: The masthead standfirst/dek states the exact number the interactive hero exists to make the reader PRODUCE ("Our model gives Argentina a 26.3% chance …"), so when the reader reaches the explorable/guess-then-reveal there is no reveal left — the centerpiece's whole payoff was handed away in the dek.
pitfalls.root_cause: The standfirst was written to summarise the finding rather than to PRIME the question + stakes. It is the same failure the Editor's 'standfirst primes, never pre-spoils' rule guards, applied to the Copywriter's masthead pass: the reveal number belongs to the interaction, not the dek.
pitfalls.fix: Write the standfirst to set up the QUESTION + the STAKES and stop there — name the model, the scale, the conflict, the invitation ('Pick a side and watch the favourite emerge'), but NOT the reveal number the hero makes the reader produce. (Mirror the Editor's standfirst rule; the Copywriter owns the masthead string, the Editor owns the body.) The reveal number stays in the interaction (read from the model, PIT-42), surfaced when the reader acts.

pitfalls.title: Caption labels an axis (or opens 'This chart shows') instead of stating the finding — the most-read line under a chart is wasted
pitfalls.symptom: A figure/photo/table caption restates what the reader can already see instead of asserting the takeaway: 'Figure 3: championship probabilities', 'the x-axis shows year', 'This chart shows the relationship between …', or the wire-caption cliché 'a stadium is pictured recently'. The caption — the most-read line under a visual — carries no conclusion, no metric/unit, no date.
pitfalls.root_cause: The caption was treated as a label, not a title. A caption IS a title: its job is to state the finding (chart = conclusion title-line + metric subtitle + source-below; photo = present-tense who/what/where + absolute date, then past-tense why; table = a 'what to look for' line). Axis-labelling and 'This chart shows…' are the caption-flavoured AI-tells.
pitfalls.fix: Run the Copywriter takeaway-title caption rule: CHART caption's title line = the conclusion (<=10 words, active, with the number), a descriptive subtitle carries the metric/unit/time/geography, the source sits below, and the outlier is annotated ON the chart (dataviz annotation_layers.json — the caption asserts, the annotation locates). PHOTO = two sentences (present-tense who/what/where + an ABSOLUTE date, then past-tense why the pixels can't show), captioning only what is depicted. TABLE caption above + a 'what to look for' line. FORBIDDEN openers: 'This chart/figure shows', 'the x/y-axis shows', 'is pictured/poses/looks on', 'may suggest a possible…', 'Figure N:'. The Copywriter writes copywriter.json items[des_xx].caption; the Programmer renders the figcaption verbatim.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — checks.json check_15_titling_caption_quality greps <figcaption> for the forbidden openers ('Figure \d', 'This (chart|figure) shows', 'the x-axis', 'the y-axis', 'is pictured', 'poses', 'looks on', 'may suggest a possible') and for a caption that is an axis label rather than a finding. Critic — corroborates via rubric.json narrative_pacing.titling_caption_cap (an axis-only caption caps narrative_pacing at 3, send back to copywriter). ADVISORY (soft) — not a validate.py kind yet.

pitfalls.title: PROJECT_DIR created before Stage 0 (input dispatch) resolves DATA_NAME — a literal top-to-bottom read of the orchestrator builds the run folder with an unresolved name
pitfalls.symptom: In URL/IDEA mode the run folder lands at a broken path: PROJECT_DIR is created as `.../{DATA_NAME}/...` with the literal placeholder still in it (or an empty/garbage segment), because the orchestrator's 'Create PROJECT_DIR' action ran before the dataset that defines DATA_NAME existed. Every later `{DATA_DIR}`/`{DATA_NAME}`-relative path (Archival, role JSONs, verify/) is then rooted under the wrong folder.
pitfalls.root_cause: The orchestrator lists 'Create PROJECT_DIR' and `PROJECT_DIR = .../{DATA_NAME}/...` as steps that DEPEND on DATA_NAME, but in URL/IDEA mode DATA_NAME is only known AFTER Stage 0 (input dispatch — ideation/find-data) resolves DATA_DIR + DATA_NAME. A reader (or an agent) who executes the orchestrator literally top-to-bottom reaches the PROJECT_DIR creation before Stage 0 has run, so the name it interpolates is still the unresolved `{DATA_NAME}` template. The ordering dependency is real but was not gated.
pitfalls.fix: Stage 0 (input dispatch) MUST resolve DATA_DIR + DATA_NAME FIRST — before ANY PROJECT_DIR creation or Archival step that interpolates `{DATA_NAME}`. Treat input acquisition as a hard prerequisite barrier: in folder/CSV mode DATA_NAME is known immediately, but in URL/IDEA mode NOTHING that references `{DATA_NAME}` (Create PROJECT_DIR, PROJECT_DIR=, Archival, any role-JSON path) may run until ideation/find-data has returned a validated DATA_DIR and DATA_NAME is set from it. WHENEVER an upstream input-acquisition stage is ADDED, gate every `{DATA_NAME}`-dependent action on that stage having run (an explicit 'DATA_NAME resolved?' precondition), so the dependency can never be satisfied by the template default.
pitfalls.detect: Orchestrator/pipeline — manual: in URL/IDEA mode confirm Stage 0 emitted a resolved DATA_DIR + DATA_NAME BEFORE any PROJECT_DIR is created; a PROJECT_DIR path still containing a literal `{DATA_NAME}` (or an empty name segment) means the creation ran ahead of input dispatch. There is no automated detector — this is an orchestrator step-ordering invariant, caught by reading the run's folder path against the stage order, not by a static check.
pitfalls.ref: data2story/SKILL.md (Stage 0 input dispatch resolves DATA_DIR/DATA_NAME before Create PROJECT_DIR + Archival; gate every {DATA_NAME}-dependent action on input acquisition having run); ideation/SKILL.md (returns the validated DATA_DIR the orchestrator sets DATA_NAME from); cf PIT-48 (a stage reading the wrong/absent source silently); (no validate.py kind — manual ordering invariant)

pitfalls.title: Idea-mode convergence + checkpoints written as free-text essays instead of AskUserQuestion choices — high-friction, and risks reading as the cold opening questionnaire
pitfalls.symptom: In IDEA mode the convergence dialogue and BOTH checkpoints ask the reader to COMPOSE prose — open-ended 'what angle do you want?' / 'is this brief OK, please describe any changes' paragraphs — instead of letting them CLICK options. The reader faces a wall of free-text prompts (high friction, easy to abandon), and if the very first turn opens with bare questions it reads as the cold opening questionnaire `sparring-partner` explicitly warns against.
pitfalls.root_cause: The idea-mode interaction was authored as conversational essay-writing rather than choice-driven selection. Picking from framed options is far lower-friction than composing, and each `AskUserQuestion` doubles as a micro-checkpoint — but that only works if the angles/scope/data-forks/approve-edit-abort decisions are presented AS options. Two failure modes compound it: (a) no 'Other / free-text' escape, so an off-menu angle (often the best one) is caged out; (b) leading the FIRST turn with options before any substance, which is the cold-questionnaire opening.
pitfalls.fix: Drive idea-mode convergence AND both checkpoints with `AskUserQuestion` (reader CLICKS): frame the angles, the scope, the data-forks, and the approve/edit/abort decisions as options, not paragraphs the reader must write. ALWAYS keep an 'Other / free-text' escape on every question — the menu is your framing, but the reader's own off-menu angle frequently wins, so it must survive. This is NOT the cold opening questionnaire `sparring-partner` warns against: lead the VERY FIRST turn with SUBSTANCE (frame the space + an open invitation), THEN switch to choice-driven options for convergence and the checkpoints. Choice-first ≠ substance-free.
pitfalls.detect: Ideation/orchestrator — manual: confirm the idea-mode convergence + Checkpoint 1 (brief) + Checkpoint 2 (dataset) are presented as `AskUserQuestion` choices each carrying an 'Other'/free-text option, and that the opening turn leads with substance before offering options (not a bare question list). There is no automated detector — this is an interaction-style judgement on the ideation dialogue, not a static grep.
pitfalls.ref: ideation/SKILL.md ('Interaction style — let the reader CHOOSE' + CHECKPOINT 1 / CHECKPOINT 2 use AskUserQuestion with an Other escape); ideation/references/sparring_brief.md (frame-with-substance-first, not a cold questionnaire); (no validate.py kind — manual interaction-style judgement)

pitfalls.title: Keyboard activation opens a popup/changes state but does NOT update the readout — mouse and keyboard disagree
pitfalls.symptom: A map marker / control responds to the MOUSE (hover/click updates the live `[data-play-out]` readout) but a KEYBOARD gesture (focus + Enter/Space/Arrow) does not update that same readout — the keyboard user sees a popup open or a visual change, yet the readout the mouse path drives stays frozen. The two input paths produce different output.
pitfalls.root_cause: The keyboard handler calls only `openPopup()` / a visual change and NEVER the readout-update fn the mouse path calls, so the `[data-play-out]` value is only ever touched on the mouse branch. Compounding it, Leaflet markers and other `[tabindex]` controls fall OUTSIDE a naive `button,input,select,textarea` interactive probe, so an a11y/keyboard check that only walks those four tags never sees the marker and the gap ships silently.
pitfalls.fix: Wire BOTH a `focus` listener AND a `keydown(Enter/Space/Arrow)` listener on the marker/control to the SAME readout-update fn the mouse path calls (so focus-or-key updates `[data-play-out]` exactly as hover/click does) — NOT only `marker.openPopup()`. Transfer the hero-halves keydown pattern (component_implementations.json `interactive_hero` wiring_js: the `el.addEventListener('keydown', …Enter/Space…)` on a `tabindex=0` `role=link` element, guarded by `vOn()`) to the marker. Give each marker `tabindex=0` + `role="button"` + an `aria-label`, and size `.leaflet-control a` to >=44px so the zoom +/- controls clear the keyboard/touch hit-area.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor Playtester `playtest_drive.js` a11y/keyboard-readout-parity check emits `interaction_keyboard_no_readout` when a keyboard gesture (focus + Enter/Space/Arrow) leaves `[data-play-out]` unchanged while the mouse path updates it. (Programmer reads this before building maps/markers.) Real-browser only — enforced by the Playtester driving a live DOM (a focus + key event), NOT by the static contract gate, which cannot drive a keyboard event.

pitfalls.title: Vega guide text (subtitle / axis / legend) falls to Vega's DARK default and goes invisible on the always-on dark cinematic background
pitfalls.symptom: A chart's title shows but its SUBTITLE (and/or axis labels, axis titles, legend text) is invisible — dark ink on the dark cinematic stage. The chart-card surface is dark, the data marks render, but the guide text is unreadable. The chart looks fine in a light-background preview, so it ships unnoticed.
pitfalls.root_cause: Vega-Lite guide-text colors default to a DARK ink. The Data2Story page is always-on dark (the cinematic stage is unconditional) and embedChart sets spec.background='transparent', so any guide-text color left unset renders dark-on-dark. The shared _config_block historically set axis label/title ink for a LIGHT frame and carried NO config.title block at all, so config.title.subtitleColor was never set — the subtitle took Vega's dark default. (subtitleColor is a SEPARATE property from title.color: setting only color still leaves the subtitle dark.) WHY IT SHIPPED: the guide-text colors were set PER-CHART / incompletely instead of in the ONE shared base config the charts share — the WC blog's 10 charts shared one embed() base config that set title.color (light) but OMITTED subtitleColor, so EVERY subtitle was dark-on-dark, yet validate.py Section 17 PASSED because Section 17 only checks whether `subtitleColor` appears ANYWHERE on the page and one OTHER chart happened to set it locally. Per-chart guide-text color is exactly how a chart gets missed — the omission hides behind any single chart that got it right.
pitfalls.fix: Put guide-text colors in the ONE shared chart base config, NEVER per-chart — per-chart (or 'one chart sets it') is precisely how a subtitle/axis/legend gets missed (the WC failure mode: 10 charts on one base config, subtitleColor omitted there, every subtitle invisible, the page-wide §17 token-presence check fooled by a single other chart). Author EVERY chart's Vega config for the dark stage from the ONE dark _config_block (dataviz-craft/references/axis_label_polish.json) so all charts INHERIT it and none can be missed: that shared block sets config.title.color + config.title.subtitleColor (both — subtitleColor is separate), config.axis.labelColor + titleColor, config.legend.labelColor + titleColor (all light, e.g. #ffffff / #e8e8e8), and light-on-dark gridColor/domainColor. Never ship a chart relying on Vega's default guide-text colors over the cinematic background, and never set these inks on individual charts in place of the shared config. The opaque .chart-card surface gives a dark backing but does NOT set the text color — that is the config's job.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py Section 17 raises `vega_dark_text_missing` when an inline chart <script> sets a `subtitle` but the page declares no `subtitleColor` anywhere (ERROR on a visual/computational topic via _rsev, WARN otherwise). Auditor — vision lens sees the missing subtitle/axis text; static: grep an inline chart <script> for a `subtitle`/`title` with no `subtitleColor`/`labelColor`/`titleColor`. The dark _config_block is the structural fix that prevents it.

pitfalls.title: Pyodide's 32-bit numpy throws casting int64->int32 (np.bincount + platform-intp index sinks) — a verify cell that runs locally fails in the browser
pitfalls.symptom: A runnable verify cell that works in local 64-bit Python/Jupyter throws in the in-browser 'Run' (Pyodide) with `TypeError: Cannot cast array data from dtype('int64') to dtype('int32') according to the rule 'safe'`. Most often np.bincount(arr) on an int64 array; any function needing platform-intp indices (fancy-index counts) can hit it.
pitfalls.root_cause: Pyodide's numpy is a 32-bit wasm build: np.intp / the default int is int32. np.bincount (and other intp-index sinks) require platform-intp indices, so an int64 array is rejected under the 'safe' casting rule. On desktop numpy (64-bit) np.intp IS int64, so the identical code passes locally and the failure only appears in the browser proof.
pitfalls.fix: Author every runnable cell Pyodide-safe for dtype: cast index args to np.intp — `np.bincount(np.asarray(x, dtype=np.intp), ...)` (np.intp is int64 on desktop = a no-op; int32 under Pyodide = fixes the throw). More generally, never assume 64-bit int in a runnable cell. AND smoke-test each runnable cell in REAL Pyodide (the in-page 'Run' button), not just local Python — local success does not prove in-browser success.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py Section 18 raises `pyodide_int64_dtype_trap` when a runnable run_cells cell calls np.bincount( on an arg not wrapped in np.intp/dtype=np.intp/.astype(np.intp) (ERROR on a computational topic via _rsev, WARN otherwise). Auditor — checks.json check_7 greps verify/run_cells.json runnable code for `np.bincount(` without an np.intp cast. (No automated in-browser execution gate exists — the real proof is a manual 'Run' click in Pyodide; the static grep covers the OBSERVED sink, not every intp-sink function.)
