pitfalls.title: A conditional/encoding object placed directly on a Vega-Lite MARK property is invalid — it fails silently (text labels lose their x/y binding and clump at the axis)
pitfalls.symptom: Text/point labels are mispositioned — they clump at the axis or ignore their x/y — with no error thrown. The spec 'looks' right but a mark property was written as `{condition:{test:…}}` / `{value:…}` instead of a literal.
pitfalls.root_cause: Mark properties (align, dx, dy, color, opacity, size, baseline, …) accept ONLY literal values in Vega-Lite. A `{condition:…}` / encoding-style object belongs on an ENCODING channel, not on `mark`. Put on `mark`, it is invalid and silently ignored / mis-applied, so e.g. text labels lose their positional binding.
pitfalls.fix: Use LITERAL mark properties only (`"align":"left"`, `"dx":4`). For per-datum styling, do it the valid way: split the data into FILTERED LAYERS (one layer per condition, each with its own literal mark props), or move the conditional onto a real ENCODING channel (`encoding.color.condition`, etc.) where `condition` IS valid. Never put `{condition:…}`/an encoding object on a mark.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py Section 19 raises `vega_conditional_on_mark` when a chart <script> has a `condition` token inside a `mark` object literal (ERROR on a visual/computational topic via _rsev, WARN otherwise). Auditor — vision lens sees text/points clumped at the axis; static: grep inline chart specs for `"mark":{…condition…}` / a `{condition:` on align/dx/dy/color.
pitfalls.ref: programmer/references/component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite.pitfalls (mark props are literals; conditionals go on encoding channels or filtered layers); dataviz-craft/references/encoding_craft.json (per-datum styling via encoding/layers); inspector/scripts/validate.py Section 19 (vega_conditional_on_mark); cf PIT-05 (NaN value-accessor), PIT-55 (a chart throw cascades)

pitfalls.title: Point/scatter marks overflow the chart frame — data beyond scale.domain draws over the axis / outside the card, and the mark isn't clipped
pitfalls.symptom: Dots/points in a scatter or dot-plot float OUTSIDE the plotting area — over the axis, the chart-card edge, or the bare background — because their value exceeds the explicit scale.domain and the mark is not clipped.
pitfalls.root_cause: An explicit scale.domain was set tighter than the data extent (or with no headroom), and the point/scatter mark has no `clip:true`. Unlike bars/areas (bounded by the baseline), points are positioned freely, so any datum past the domain renders outside the frame.
pitfalls.fix: Two-part: (1) give scale.domain HEADROOM past the data max/min, or OMIT domain so Vega auto-fits the extent; AND (2) set `clip:true` on the point/scatter mark so nothing ever draws outside the plot frame. clip is the belt, domain headroom the suspenders.
pitfalls.detect: Auditor — vision/render lens sees points outside the plot or over the card edge (the real catch). Static (smell, not a gate): grep a point/scatter chart spec for an explicit `scale`/`domain` on the point axis with NO `clip:true` on the mark. NOT statically decidable as a hard gate — whether a point overflows depends on the DATA vs the domain, which validate.py cannot evaluate without running the chart, so there is intentionally no validate.py kind; the authoring rule + the render lens carry it.
pitfalls.ref: dataviz-craft/references/axis_label_polish.json point_overflow_rule (clip:true + domain headroom); programmer/references/component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite.pitfalls (point marks: clip + headroom); auditor render/vision lens; cf PIT-03 (the OUTER svg axis/legend overhead overflows its card — a different case, fixed by svg_must_fit), PIT-01 (0-width)

pitfalls.title: A 'share my result' button using the Web Share API (navigator.share/canShare with a File) crashes the whole browser tab — a renderer-process crash try/catch cannot intercept
pitfalls.symptom: Clicking a 'share / copy my result' button kills the ENTIRE Chrome tab — 'Aw, Snap!', `Error code: RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE`. Not a thrown JS error: the try/catch around the call and the promise `.catch()` BOTH fail to fire (the page is gone, not the function). Hits hardest when previewing the blog locally on a `file://` origin.
pitfalls.root_cause: Handing the Web Share API a File payload — `navigator.share({files:[file]})` / `navigator.canShare({files})` — makes the renderer send the browser an IPC the browser process REJECTS, which kills the renderer (RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE). It is a renderer-process crash, BELOW the JS layer, so `try/catch` and promise `.catch()` cannot catch it. A `file://` origin (how authors preview blogs locally) is the most reliable trigger, but some https Chrome builds hit it too. The crash surface is the Web Share API File path itself, not a recoverable exception.
pitfalls.fix: Do NOT use the Web Share API for any 'share / copy result' feature — there is no try/catch that makes it safe. Instead: copy the result CARD IMAGE to the clipboard via `navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'image/png': blob, 'text/plain': textBlob})])` (pastes as a PICTURE into chat/social AND as TEXT into text fields), with a `navigator.clipboard.writeText` fallback and an ALWAYS-present Download link as the universal floor. Build the image Blob SYNCHRONOUSLY (`canvas.toDataURL('image/png')` -> Blob, NOT async `canvas.toBlob`) so the clipboard write runs INSIDE the click's user-activation window — an async toBlob defers past the activation and the clipboard write then rejects. Never leak a `file://` URL in the share text: gate any URL placed in the text payload to http(s) origins only. This clipboard-copy + download path delivers the same 'Share / Copy my result' result on every platform with ZERO crash surface.
pitfalls.detect: Inspector/pipeline — validate.py Section 20 raises `web_share_api_used` when an inline <script> body calls `navigator.share(`/`navigator.canShare(` (WARN — advises clipboard.write([ClipboardItem]) + writeText fallback + Download link, build the Blob synchronously, http(s)-only share URL). Auditor — manual: click any share/copy control in a real browser AND on a file:// preview and confirm the tab does not crash; static: grep inline <script> for `navigator.share(`/`navigator.canShare(` (expect the clipboard-copy + download pattern instead). Reference implementation: the WC blog `wirePickerAndShare`/`doShare`/`clipboardFallback` (synchronous toDataURL->Blob, ClipboardItem image+text, writeText fallback, download-card, no Web Share API).
